43522060.article_content:
The Classic 2 is a brand new revision of the original Classic, and kits are available today starting at
$144CAD
!
The Classic 2 is just like the original in every way that matters. It’s also a major upgrade for the few things that needed tweaking.
Check out the shop
USB-C connector
That’s right, the Classic 2 has a USB-C connector!
The original Classic has a bulky USB-B connector on it (if you don’t know, it’s the connector that you often find in printers). USB-B connectors are very mechanically strong, a quality we prioritised for the purposes of longevity.
Since we launched the original Classic, we’ve been shipping many devices with USB-C connectors. We’ve shown to ourselves that these connectors are just as reliable and strong as USB-B connectors.
So, yes – the Classic 2 will have a USB-C connector on it, and it’ll be just as mechanically strong as the connector on the original Classic.
An improved scroll wheel
A common issue with the original Classic was that the scroll wheel would often act oddly if spun too quickly, or would sometimes reverse direction unexpectedly. This issue arose from the way the scroll wheel works.
Want the gory technical details? Expand to find out more.
The scroll wheel operates using something called a “binary Gray code”.
The binary Gray code is simply a way of seeing the direction in which something is moving. If you’ve ever been to a parking garage that has a parking space counter, it’s usually implemented as a binary Gray code.
The way it works is that two lasers are positioned at the entrance to the garage. If, for example, a car breaks the first beam and then the second, the garage’s software knows that a car is entering. If the second beam is broken and then the first, a car is leaving. Our scroll wheel is implemented in a very similar way.
The scroll wheel design uses a phototransistor to detect the “laser” (which is actually an infrared photodiode, in our case). The microcontroller polls the phototransistor to see if it’s detecting any light.
And this is the key problem: the detection poll. The microcontroller in the original Classic is very, very slow. It runs at just 8MHz, which means that if the scroll wheel is spun too quickly, the microcontroller can’t keep up.
In our parking garage analogy, it’s as if multiple cars pass through the laser beams very fast. If the garage’s software is too slow, it’ll think only one car entered the garage. That’s exactly what’s happening in our scroll wheel, since the microcontroller is too slow.
The good news is that we put a new microcontroller in the Classic 2: the Raspberry RP2040. This new microcontroller runs the scroll wheel algorithms fifteen times faster than the one in the original Classic.
The result is crisp, accurate scrolling without any spinouts or unexpected reversals.
Same great shape and performance, with improved printability
The ergonomics of the original Classic were something that we really worked hard on, and many people agree that it works well. Because of that, we didn’t change the ergonomics, at all.
The Classic 2 has exactly the same shape. We promise – we didn’t mess with it in the slightest!
We did, however, change it to make it more printable. The original Classic had some odd overhangs and support material requirements that we’ve worked out of the design.
So, now, the same great ergonomic shape should roll off your printer much more smoothly than before.
We also kept all of the high-performance harware inside. The Classic 2 still has the great PMW-3360 optical sensor for unparalleled accuracy, and still uses great D2LS-21 switches for fantastic clicks.
learn more
And… still open-source
Of course, the entire Classic 2 design is open-source, under the CERN OHL license for the hardware and GPL for the firmware.
We’ve also released full assembly documentation and everything you’d need to build a kit, repair it, make one yourself, or mod it.
Go to the Github Repository
Thanks to everyone in our community!
We’re excited to share this with you, and we hope that the Classic 2 will serve this community well. We’re looking forward to seeing your builds and mods in the future!
Stay in touch with us!
Reddit
Mastodon
GitHub
Mail
Frequently Asked Questions
Do you have an upgrade kit so I can upgrade my original Classic to a Classic 2?
Unfortunately, no. The original Classic PCBs weren’t designed to be upgraded at a later date, so it’s not possible to swap in the new components for the old ones. Additionally, almost all of the plastic parts have been updated, so the Classic 2 parts aren’t compatible with the original Classic.
Will you continue selling original Classic kits?
No, the original Classic design will be retired from our shop.
Will you continue providing maintenance kits for the original Classic?
Yes! We will continue providing support in the form of maintenance kits to everybody who supported us by purchasing an original Classic kit.

不同观点：
• [ethanol-brain] 认为实验中啮齿动物每天暴露于乙醇蒸汽16小时，持续数周，这种实验条件过于极端，类似于人类的狂饮行为，质疑其实际应用价值。
• [greenavocado] 强调实验结果的持久性，指出雄性大鼠在停止接触乙醇10周后仍表现出差异，暗示可能有长期的生理影响，即使在戒酒后依然存在。
• [tombert] 分享了个人经历，提到自己在戒酒后感到某种难以形容的变化，并怀疑这种变化可能是生理上的影响，而不仅仅是心理作用，尽管其样本量小且个人化。
• [Jun8] 对实验中观察到的性别差异表示兴趣，引用研究指出这些差异并非由于生理特性，而是其他因素，如荷尔蒙或染色体差异，并对此提出疑问。
• [nagaiaida] 批评研究中对“性别依赖”的定义不够明确，指出需要更深入理解是染色体差异还是内分泌因素导致了这些差异。
• [wnevets] 简单直接地认为酒精本质上就是毒药，对实验结果并不感到意外。
• [rickydroll] 以幽默方式提到“啤酒眼镜”效应（指喝酒后对人外貌判断改变），偏离了严肃讨论。

data.title: Are people bad at their jobs or are the jobs just bad?
data.author: moonka
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：工作环境、劳动条件、以及工作质量之间的关系，特别是针对现代工作压力和 gig 经济（零工经济）中的问题。

不同观点：
• **工作压力与效率的矛盾**：[rqtwteye] 认为现代工作环境对效率的过度追求导致员工没有足够的时间和精力做好工作。他以90年代软件开发的实验时间为例，说明如今员工被要求快速完成任务，缺少自主空间，导致工作质量下降。他还提到 Google 曾推行的“20%时间”政策（允许员工花一部分时间做自己想做的项目），认为这种灵活性有助于产生好成果。

• **gig 经济的问题**：[brudgers] 指出 gig 经济中的员工无法在公司中获得职业发展，也无法建立人际网络，甚至可能与同事形成竞争关系。这与传统工作环境相比更加没有前途。

• **平台经济的适用性**：[protocolture] 观察到一些在平台上全职工作的 gig 工作者为了快速完成任务而牺牲质量。他认为这些平台更适合那些利用闲暇时间接单的专业人士，而非全职依赖这些平台的人。

• **平台服务质量低下的原因**：[Uzmanali] 分享了自己对 gig 平台的失望经历，指出这些平台不支持高技能、高薪酬的工人，反而注重廉价和便捷，导致工作质量低下。他选择雇佣本地专业人士，即使价格更高，但节省了时间和 frustration。

• **低薪与低质量工作的恶性循环**：[ryandrake] 认为 gig 工作和低薪、低技能的服务工作之间存在恶性循环。这些工作本身不尽如人意，愿意从事这些工作的人往往也不太满意、技能不高，导致工作质量进一步下降。

• **劳动法与企业责任**：[cadamsdotcom] 批评美国的劳动法过时且执行不力，企业为了盈利会尽可能剥削员工。他建议提高某些岗位的工资，并引入追责机制以改善现状。

• **文化差异与劳动价值观**：[wnolens] 指出北美消费者重视廉价商品和服务，不太关心背后的劳动条件，这种文化导致了对低质量劳动的容忍。

• **培训与工作质量的关系**：[lesuorac] 认为如果员工没有接受适当培训，期望他们做好工作是不合理的。他以苹果和 UPS 的培训为例，说明系统化的培训能够提高工作表现。

• **管理与工作成果的关系**：[OutOfHere] 认为在软件行业中，管理者的角色可以通过用户数量来衡量。如果开发者的工作没有用户使用，往往是管理者的责任。

• **高工资是否提升工作质量的争议**：[ckdot] 提到在德国，尽管有较高的最低工资和严格的劳动法保护，工人的工作质量并没有显著提高。他质疑高工资是否必然带来工作质量的提升。

补充讨论：
• **退休经验分享**：[zw123456] 分享了自己在科技行业45年的工作经验，强调不要害怕在职场中表现得与众不同，勇敢面对工作环境中的挑战。

• **对过去工作环境的怀旧**：[cynicalsecurity] 认为过去的工作节奏较慢，对员工和地球都有益处，现代社会应该适当放慢节奏。

争议焦点：高工资是否能有效提升工作质量，以及 gig 经济平台是否适合作为全职工作依赖。

data.title: Switzerland's vinyl turntable roundabout: Unique road art (2019)
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 瑞士吕斯镇（Lyss） near 伯尔尼最近建造了一个独特的环岛，形状如同一个巨大的黑胶唱片转盘，直径12米，唱片部分直径10米，侧面装有800个银色金属垫圈。虽然它不会旋转或发出声音，且缺少唱臂，但其设计引人注目。该环岛由伯尔尼土木工程部门委托建造，位于通往文化工厂（Kulturfabrik, KUFA）的公路入口处，KUFA是一个举办派对、跳蚤市场、 pub quiz和文化活动的热门场所。经过多年规划，这个名为KUFA Kreisel的环岛于2019年5月完工，迅速在网络上走红。环岛设计最初曾考虑过集装箱涂鸦艺术和超大麦克风等方案，但最终选择了与环岛形状契合的巨型转盘设计。这个独特的交通景观成为了前往KUFA参加活动的理由之一。

不同观点：
• MatthiasWandel认为圆点间距应根据不同的电频率（50Hz和60Hz）以及不同的转速（33.33RPM和45RPM）有所变化。他指出，应该有四组不同的圆点环，每组圆点数不同以反映这些差异。
• 另一种潜在的观点（未在评论中明确表达）可能是，圆点间距不必严格对应不同的频率和转速，可能出于设计简化或视觉效果的考虑，所有圆点间距可以一致。

补充讨论：
• MatthiasWandel提出了具体的参数，即四种不同的设置：50Hz和60Hz的电频率以及33.33RPM和45RPM的转速，这表明他对于技术准确性有一定的期望。
• 争议焦点在于是否需要为了技术准确性而改变圆点间距，还是可以为了简化设计而保持一致间距。
• 该评论还暗示了设计和功能之间的潜在冲突，即设计者可能为了美观或简单而忽略了一些技术细节，而MatthiasWandel显然更看重准确性。

Switzerland’s Vinyl Turntable Roundabout: Unique Road Art
Dimitri Burkhard
May 24, 2019
2 min read
Share
Tweet
81
Share
Pin
52
WhatsApp
133
Shares
Switzerland's flag may be square, but its streets are dotted with roundabouts.
About as ordinary as station clocks, every town has at least one. And since the public is often involved in designing these traffic circles, we have seen horrible things... Think horizontal steel pipes or piles of rock.
But all is not lost, as the town of Lyss near Bern proves. Those who swing by will undoubtedly hit the latest roundabout. And given its decor, does it surprise that the KUFA Kreisel has gone viral?
This roundabout in Switzerland is a giant vinyl turntable.
It doesn’t spin or produce any sounds. Heck, it is missing a tonearm! Even though the traffic circle in Lyss is quite an eye-catcher...
Credits go to the Bern civil engineering department, which had commissioned the roundabout.
The KUFA Kreisel is located at a freeway entrance near a popular cultural venue called
Kulturfabrik
. Its club hosts frequent parties, but the KUFA also offers flea markets, pub quizzes, and cultural events.
It made sense for the creative folks at KUFA to be in charge of designing their roundabout. And after years of planning, the traffic circle was completed in May 2019.
I love the idea of a turntable with a branded vinyl record.
The roundabout has a total diameter of 12 meters, with the record alone being 10 meters. Attached to its side are 800 silver metal washers. According to a person involved, the initial idea was to install a cargo container featuring graffiti art. Another idea was to place an oversized microphone in the center.
From there, the idea of a record player was not too far. But given the roundabout’s circular shape, it made more sense to design a gigantic turntable.
So there you have it: a great reason to swing by the town of Lyss between Biel and Bern. Give this traffic circle a spin before leaving the roundabout for a concert at the KUFA...
While you're at it, check out Switzerland's
record player stamp
or have a look at this
experimental video clip
. providing a new perspective on the roundabout.
(Photograph copyright KUFA Kulturfabrik)

data.title: Show HN: Color palettes inspired by Mexican architecture
data.author: sillysideprojs
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一个色彩项目的不同角度评价与联想

不同观点：
• **支持并建议扩展形式**：[keiferski] 认为该项目很酷，并建议考虑将其发展为一本书。他提到最近购买了一本类似的关于日本传统色彩组合的书，提供了相关链接，显示出对色彩主题出版物的兴趣和支持。

• **技术性疑问**：[jslakro] 对项目的技术实现提出了疑问，猜测颜色是否是通过程序从照片中提取出来的，显示出对项目背后技术实现的关注。

• **与其他内容的关联与思考**：[bryanrasmussen] 提到该项目出现在一篇关于“世界为何失去色彩”的文章下方，不确定这是否构成反驳论点，还是仅仅是一个有趣的并列。这显示出对项目内容与更广泛文化讨论之间关系的思考。

补充讨论：
• [bryanrasmussen] 的评论引出了一个值得注意的讨论点，即该色彩项目是否可以视作对“世界失去色彩”论点的反驳或是补充，这涉及到项目内容的文化与社会意义。

• 不同评论者对项目的关注点各异，有的注重形式和扩展（出书），有的关注技术实现，还有的将项目置于更广泛的文化讨论中。

43542804.article_content:
Skip to content
Article
In the Matter of the Commas
For the true literary stylist, this seemingly humble punctuation mark is a matter of precision, logic, individuality, and music
By
Matthew Zipf
|
March 3, 2025
Photo of Renata Adler by WWD/Getty Images
1.
At the Art Institute of Chicago, Joan Didion and her daughter, Quintana, were looking at a painting by Georgia O’Keeffe. The work,
Sky Above Clouds IV,
hung across a landing, so they had a gulf of air between themselves and the flat white shapes that span a long wall at the museum. It is a giant painting, practically a mural, as wide as the abstract Barnett Newman canvases that you can walk along and let fill the whole of your vision. But this work floats at a distance, celestially, and you just look out at it. There are 192 square feet of clouds. You are in an airplane. “Who drew it?” Quintana whispered to her mother. “I need to talk to her.” On which Didion reflected, in her 1979 essay collection
The White Album:
My daughter was making, that day in Chicago, an entirely unconscious but quite basic assumption about people and the work they do. She was assuming … that the painting was the painter as the poem is the poet, that every choice one made alone—every word chosen or rejected, every brush stroke laid or not laid down—betrayed one’s character.
Style is character
.
Didion held on to that belief throughout her career. How you write or paint is who you are, she thought. Sometimes she went further. Style not only showed your character but, as she wrote in a late novel, might even reveal your politics, your ideas about the world—what you had come to think and believe.
In his review of
The White Album
for
The London Review of Books,
Martin Amis mocked the scene with Quintana at the Art Institute. Style had nothing to do with character, he wrote. It was a ridiculous notion. In Chicago, Didion showed “how quickly sentimentality proceeds to nonsense,” Amis wrote. “If style were character, everyone would write as self-revealingly as Miss Didion. Not everyone does.” Plenty of writers remain anonymous, or produce books that seemingly have little to do with their real lives. Didion had fallen in love with an idea that could not withstand scrutiny, according to Amis. “The extent to which style isn’t character,” he wrote, “can be gauged by (for example) reading a literary biography, or by trying to imagine a genuinely fruitful discussion between Georgia O’Keeffe and Miss Didion’s seven-year-old daughter.”
2.
The most conspicuous mark of Renata Adler’s style is its abundance of commas. In her two novels,
Speedboat
(1976) and
Pitch Dark
(1983), there are a few sentences that edge on the absurd: “For some time, Leander had spoken, on the phone, of a woman, a painter, whom he had met, one afternoon, outside the gym, and whom he was trying to introduce, along with Simon, into his apartment and his life.” A critic tallied it up, counting “40 words and ten commas—
Guinness Book of World Records?
” Each of those commas had its grammatical defense, but Adler’s style did not comply with the usual standards of fluent prose. She cordoned off phrases, such as “on the phone,” that other writers would just run through. One reader, responding to a 1983
New York
magazine profile of Adler, wrote in a letter to the editor, “If the examples of Renata Adler’s writing … are typical, Miss Adler will never make it to the road. The way is ‘jarringly, piece by piece, line by line, and without interruption’ blocked by commas.” The reader was quoting one of Adler’s own comma-laden critical phrases against her. The editors titled the letter “Comma Wealth.”
Adler’s comma usage differs from the balanced rhythms of 18th-century essayists, as well as from the breathless lines common among American writers after Hemingway. Her punctuation jars, and turns abruptly, like a skater’s blade stopping and sending up shards of ice. She likes to leave out conjunctions in chains of adjectives, as in her film review of  “a leering, uncertain, embarrassing, protracted little comedy.” Certain lines of hers work almost entirely by carefully placed commas, which tighten the style, each one a rivet on the page: “But this I know, or think I know, that idle people are often bored and bored people, unless they sleep a lot, are cruel.” A hesitation, a stutter, and then a swing into the qualification (“unless they sleep a lot”). Interestingly, no comma in “bored and bored people”: grammar sacrificed for rhythm and speed.
Not everyone saw the elegant precision in how she pointed her sentences. After one of her books came out, a critic wrote that “virtually every sentence is peppered with enough commas to make the prose read like a series of hiccups.” Another letter writer complained of her “muddled syntax and wandering, endless sentences.”
But Adler’s style had its admirers, too. “Nobody in this country writes better prose than Renata Adler’s,” a critic wrote in a
Harper’s
review of her first novel.

data.title: What We Knew Without Knowing
data.author: apollinaire
data.article_summary: Joan Didion and John Gregory Dunne, both writers, had a deeply collaborative marriage. Following Didion's death in 2021, the New York Public Library opened their archive, which includes Didion's typewritten notes from therapy sessions with psychiatrist Roger MacKinnon starting in 1999. These notes, addressed to Dunne, discuss Didion's concerns about their adopted daughter Quintana's struggles with depression and alcoholism, as well as her own fears about aging and creativity. Didion reflects on her anxiety and the dynamics of their family, capturing her thoughts with her signature clarity. The notes will be published as "Notes to John" and provide insight into the themes of loss and anxiety that are also present in Didion's memoirs, "The Year of Magical Thinking" and "Blue Nights," written after Dunne's and Quintana's deaths.

Joan Didion and John Gregory Dunne met in the late fifties, when she was working at Vogue and he at Time. They married in 1964, and in 1966 they adopted a baby girl, giving her a name from the Yucatán: Quintana Roo. Together, Didion and Dunne lived out one of the most collaborative literary marriages in American history. Last week, after two years of preparation, the New York Public Library opened the Didion-Dunne archive to the public. Among its three hundred and thirty-six boxes of material is a thick file of typewritten notes by Didion describing her sessions with the psychiatrist Roger MacKinnon, beginning in 1999. Addressed to Dunne, the entries are full of direct quotations and written with the immediacy of fresh recollection. Didion was concerned about Quintana and her struggles with depression and alcoholism, but she was preoccupied, too, with aging, with creative fulfillment, with the complex dynamics of their family. She recorded her thoughts with the cool, forensic clarity she was known for. These entries will be published in book form as “Notes to John.” Readers of her memoirs “The Year of Magical Thinking,” written in the wake of Dunne’s sudden death, in 2003, at the age of seventy-one, and “Blue Nights,” about Quintana’s death less than two years later, at thirty-nine, will recognize how these notes inform those final books—the striving to understand and the sense of futility that comes with it. “Life changes fast,” Didion famously wrote. “Life changes in the instant. You sit down to dinner and life as you know it ends.” She died in 2021, at eighty-seven.
—
David Remnick
29 December 1999
Re not taking Zoloft, I said it made me feel for about an hour after taking it that I’d lost my organizing principle, rather like having a planters’ punch before lunch in the tropics. I said I’d tried to think this through, because I knew rationally it couldn’t be true, since the PDR said even twice that dose doesn’t reach any effect for several hours and peak effect for 3-5 days of steady dosage. I realized that I had a very closely calibrated idea of my physical well-being, very fearful of losing control, that my personality was organized around a certain level of mobilization or anxiety.
I then said that I had tried to think through the anxiety I had expressed at our last meeting. I said that although it had been expressed in terms of work (the meeting in Los Angeles etc.), I realized when I discussed it with you that it was focused on Quintana.
“Of course it was,” he said. We then talked about what my anxieties were re Quintana. Basically, they were that she would become depressed to a point of danger. The shoe dropping, the call in the middle of the night, the attempt to take her emotional temperature on every phone call. I said that in some ways this seemed justified and in other ways unfair to her, because she must be feeling our anxiety as we were feeling hers.
“I suspect she feels your anxiety very particularly,” he said. I said apparently she did. She had not only told us she did but had also mentioned this to Dr. Kass. It was me and not you she wanted to see a psychiatrist. He said he would assume that she read anxiety in both of us, but that something in her and my relationship made her feel mine more acutely, made her lock into mine. “People with certain neurotic patterns lock into each other in a way that people with healthy patterns don’t. There’s clearly a very powerful dependency that goes both ways between you and her.”
He wanted to know how old Quintana was when we got her, the details of the adoption. We talked at some length about that, and I said I had always been afraid we would lose her. Whalewatching. The hypothetical rattlesnake in the ivy on Franklin Avenue. He said that just as all adoptive children have a deep fear that they will be given away again, all adoptive parents have a deep fear that the child will be taken from them. If you don’t deal with these fears at the time you have them, you displace them, obsessively on dangers you can control—the snake in the garden—as opposed to the danger you can’t control. “Obviously, you didn’t deal with this fear at the time. You set it aside. That’s your pattern. You move on, you muddle through, you control the situation through your work and your competency. But the fear is still there, and when you discovered this summer that your daughter was in danger you couldn’t manage or control, the fear broke through your defenses.”
I said I may have been overprotective, but I never thought she saw me that way. In fact, she once described me, as a mother, as “a little remote.”
Dr. MacKinnon: “You don’t think she saw your remoteness as a defense? When she uses remoteness herself as a defense? Didn’t you just tell me? She never looks back?”
2 February 2000
. . .

data.article_summary: ISTA的研究人员推出了一种新的脑类器官模型，该模型包含微glia细胞，用于研究病毒感染对发育中神经系统的反应，特别是风疹（Rubella）病毒。风疹在怀孕期间感染可能导致胎儿脑部畸形和成年后精神分裂症风险增加。类器官由人类诱导多能干细胞（hiPSCs）培养而成，模拟早期胎儿脑发育过程。通过将微glia整合到视网膜类器官中，研究团队观察到微glia在病毒感染引发的炎症反应中的作用，发现其引发过度炎症反应，可能干扰神经回路组装，导致神经发育缺陷。该模型对药物安全性测试，特别是孕妇用药，具有重要意义。研究结果发表在《Journal of Neuroinflammation》上。

Pink Skies
April 3, 2025
Pink Skies
ISTA researchers present new brain organoid model
Organoids have revolutionized science and medicine, providing platforms for disease modeling, drug testing, and understanding developmental processes. While not exact replicas of human organs, they offer significant insights. The Siegert group at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) presents a new organoid model that reveals details of the developing nervous system’s response to viral infections, such as Rubella. This model could influence pharmaceutical testing, particularly benefiting drug safety for pregnant women.
Pink skies.
Microglia (magenta) integrated into a retinal organoid. The cell nuclei of neurons are stained in blue. © Schmied et al. / Journal of Neuroinflammation
Microglia are special cells in the human brain. Like a diligent ranger overseeing a forest and dealing with infestations and wildfires, microglia scan the brain environment for germs and initiate an anti-inflammatory response to remove them. They also monitor the quantity of neurons (nerve cells) and their connections to ensure optimal brain function in adulthood.
Sandra Siegert and her research group at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)
focus on these microglia and their interplay with neurons during embryonic development. In their latest publication, the Siegert group introduces a new brain organoid model that, for the first time, incorporates microglia to mimic inflammatory reactions and their treatment. The results are published in the
Journal of Neuroinflammation.
Scanning cells
. Microglia (grey) are highly dynamic cells and monitor their environment by extending and retracting their processes. © Schmied et al. / Journal of Neuroinflammation
Rubella – the “German Measles”
Little itchy red dots that spread from the face across the body are a common experience for parents with children suffering from Rubella.
For kids and adults alike, the infection is mild; however, if contracted when pregnant, it can have serious implications. Rubella is classified into the so-called “TORCH-infections” (toxoplasmosis, others, rubella, cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex), which can be transmitted from a pregnant person to the developing fetus, causing malformations of the fetal brain and thus increasing the risk of schizophrenia in adulthood.
Understanding how such viral infections affect the development of the human brain is crucial. PhD student Verena Schmied, together with Professor Sandra Siegert and her research group at ISTA, set out to uncover some answers. Retinal organoids—one of the first established brain region-specific models with known developmental trajectories and cell architecture—proved to be highly useful.
3D structures that mimic the human brain
To get an organoid, you start, for instance, with skin cells from a person. These cells are then reprogrammed or ‘set back to factory setting’ to get versatile pluripotent stem cells—called human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). Given the right circumstances, hiPSCs can develop into any other cell type. With special growth factors, nutrients, and environmental constraints, hiPSCs cluster together and self-organize into mature retinal organoids in a Petri dish.
“Retinal organoids allow us to recapitulate important steps of early fetal brain development,” says Schmied. To make accurate statements, these organoids must closely resemble the real thing. Recent brain-region organoid models to test viral infections during brain development, however, did not include microglia which are usually present from very early developmental stages.
Organoid with microglia.
Microglia (magenta) integrated into retinal organoids (grey). ©Schmied et al.
To change that notion, the scientists added microglia into retinal organoids and used fluorescent colors and microscopes to verify their successful integration. Between the blue-stained neurons, the delicate bodies of microglia were prominently visible in bright pink. A beautiful moment for Siegert, who recalls, “Seeing an organoid full of integrated microglia and how they distribute themselves was really remarkable.”
What happens after a viral infection?
The researchers then investigated how their organoids acted upon viral infection. “We mimicked viral infection with a synthetic molecule, that is recognized as a viral component and compared organoids with and without microglia,” Schmied continues.
The viral infection distracts microglia properties, causing them to address this infection by inducing an inflammatory response. The shift results in an excess of dividing neurons, which could interfere with the proper assembly of the neuronal circuit, ultimately causing neurodevelopmental defects.

data.title: AI Ambivalence
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 在《Read the Tea Leaves》一文中，Nolan Lawson讨论了对生成式AI的复杂感受。作为拥有计算语言学硕士学位的开发者，Lawson回顾了自己在AI领域的经历和对其的怀疑。他提到早期AI开发主要依赖统计和数据训练，这让他感到枯燥并放弃该领域。尽管对AI持怀疑态度，他承认当前AI技术在实际任务中表现出色，尤其是在编码领域。然而，他认为AI助手常常打扰工作流程，生成难以发现的错误，并未显著提升生产力。Lawson引用Baldur Bjarnason的《The Intelligence Illusion》一书，强调AI可能降低使用者能力并产生额外工作。尽管如此，他意识到到2025年，AI的广泛应用已成为不可忽视的趋势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生成式AI对人类创造力和工作的影响

不同观点：
• crabmusket认为生成式AI传达的信息是“你是衍生的”，即人类的创造力和技艺可以被AI复制。他提到这种观点让他对人生产生了悲观的看法，并感到在软件开发中使用AI可能会削弱工作的乐趣。他个人并未广泛使用LLM（大型语言模型），但在处理一些编程问题时，偶尔会用它们替代Stack Overflow。

• thearrow对crabmusket的观点表示赞同，并批评一些软件工程师过于依赖AI生成代码，认为这是对自己认知能力的放弃，并对此表示不解和不满。

• upghost对crabmusket提到的创造力和情感被AI替代的观点表示感触很深，认为这种讨论揭示了人类可能会怀念的真实情感。

• p2detar认为这类讨论让人感受到人性的存在，并预测人们会很快意识到这种失去。

• AndrewKemendo从专业角度出发，对生成式AI的兴起表示复杂的情感。他为一些在自然语言处理（NLP）和贝叶斯方法领域工作的人感到难过，但同时也为自己在强化学习（RL）领域的进展感到高兴。他提到RL正在成为主流的智能框架，并预见AI领域将会有更多令人兴奋的发展，但也指出许多人在AI无法泛化的情况下会感到倦怠。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及的争议焦点在于生成式AI是否真的能替代人类的创造力和技艺，以及这种替代对人类工作和生活的影响。部分人对此持悲观态度，认为这会削弱工作的乐趣和人类独特性，而其他人则对技术进步表示乐观，但也承认其中的挑战和困难。

• crabmusket对使用AI生成代码的具体场景和态度提供了实际例子，如在处理复杂编程问题时会偶尔使用LLM，但整体上仍对AI持保留态度。

AI ambivalence
Posted April 2, 2025 by Nolan Lawson in
Machine Learning
,
NLP
.
7 Comments
I’ve avoided writing this post for a long time, partly because I try to avoid controversial topics these days, and partly because I was waiting to make my mind up about the current, all-consuming, conversation-dominating topic of generative AI. But Steve Yegge’s
“Revenge of the junior developer”
awakened something in me, so let’s go for it.
I don’t come to AI from nowhere. Longtime readers may be surprised to learn that I have a master’s in
computational linguistics
, i.e. I studied this kind of stuff 20-odd years ago. In fact, two of the authors of the famous
“stochastic parrot”
paper were folks I knew at the time – Emily Bender was one of my professors, and Margaret Mitchell was my lab partner in one of our toughest classes (sorry my Python sucked at the time, Meg).
That said, I got bored of working in AI after grad school, and quickly switched to general coding. I just found that “feature engineering” (which is what we called training models at the time) was not really my jam. I much preferred to put on
some good coding tunes
, crank up the IDE, and bust out code all day. Plus, I had developed a dim view of natural-language processing technologies largely informed by my background in (non-computational) linguistics as an undergrad.
In linguistics, we were taught that the human mind is a wondrous thing, and that Chomsky had conclusively shown that humans have a natural language instinct. The job of the linguist is to uncover the hidden rules in the human mind that govern things like syntax, semantics, and phonology (i.e. why the “s” in “beds” is pronounced like a “z” unlike in “bets,” due to the voicing of the final consonant).
Then when I switched to computational linguistics, suddenly the overriding sensation I got was that everything was
actually
about number-crunching, and in fact you could throw all your linguistics textbooks in the trash and just let gobs of training data and statistics do the job for you. “Every time I fire a linguist, the performance goes up,” as
a famous computational linguist
said.
I found this perspective belittling and insulting to the human mind, and more importantly, it didn’t really seem to
work
. Natural-language processing technology seemed stuck at the level of
support vector machines
and
conditional random fields
, hardly better than the Markov models in your iPhone 2’s autocomplete. So I got bored and disillusioned and left the field of AI.
Boy, that AI thing sure came back with a vengeance, didn’t it?
Still skeptical
That said, while everybody else was either reacting with horror or delight at the tidal wave of gen-AI hype, I maintained my skepticism. At the end of the day, all of this technology was still just number-crunching – brute force trying to approximate the hidden logic that Chomsky had discovered. I acknowledged that there was some room for statistics – Peter Norvig’s essay mentioning
the story of an Englishman ordering an “ale” and getting served an “eel”
due to
the Great Vowel Shift
still sticks in my brain – but overall I doubted that mere stats could ever approach anything close to human intelligence.
Today, though, philosophical questions of what AI says about human cognition seem beside the point – these things can
get stuff done
. Especially in the field of coding (my cherished refuge from computational linguistics), AIs now dominate: every IDE assumes I want AI autocomplete by default, and I actively have to hunt around in the settings to turn it off.
And for several years, that’s what I’ve been doing: studiously avoiding generative AI. Not just because I doubted how close to
“AGI”
these things actually were, but also because I just found them annoying. I’m a fast typist, and I know JavaScript like the back of my hand, so the last thing I want is some overeager junior coder grabbing my keyboard to mess with the flow of my typing. Every inline-coding AI assistant I’ve tried made me want to gnash my teeth together – suddenly instead of
writing code
, I’m being asked to constantly
read code
(which as everyone knows, is less fun). And plus, the suggestions were rarely good enough to justify the aggravation. So I abstained.
Later I read Baldur Bjarnason’s excellent book
The Intelligence Illusion
, and this further hardened me against generative AI. Why use a technology that 1) dumbs down the human using it, 2) generates hard-to-spot bugs, and 3) doesn’t really make you much more productive anyway, when you consider the extra time reading, reviewing, and correcting its output? So I put in my earbuds and kept coding.
Meanwhile, as I was blissfully coding away like it was ~2020, I looked outside my window and suddenly realized that the tidal wave was approaching. It was 2025, and I was (seemingly) the last developer on the planet not us

data.title: Ask HN: How do you make a living contributing to and/or creating OSS projects?
data.author: Brysonbw
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何通过开源软件（OSS）获得收入或维持生计

不同观点：
• nickjj：认为通过OSS直接获得捐款收入非常困难，尽管有一些项目获得了用户的感谢和少量资助，但十年来仅获得约17美元。他本人不以赚钱为目的，主要是为了回馈社区，基于个人需求开发项目并公开分享。

• benhoyt：通过为一家主要从事开源项目的公司（如Canonical）工作，来间接参与开源。虽然项目不属于个人，但工作成果是公开的。通过GitHub Sponsors获得的资助非常有限，仅够偶尔的小额消费。

• bawolff：认为除非非常有名，否则通过捐赠获得有意义的收入不太可能。建议为有相关软件需求的公司工作或做咨询来获得收入。

• matvp：由所在公司资助进行OSS贡献，个人项目则通过小额捐赠获得一定支持。曾将公司内部项目开源，并通过与项目维护者合作获得法律批准。

• ThinkBeat：认为通过OSS获得收入是不现实的，建议通过全职工作来维持生计，将OSS作为志愿者活动。提出一些项目通过改变许可和推出专业版来盈利。

• plankalkyl：没有个人经验，但引用Evan Czaplicki的演讲讨论开源编程语言的经济问题，认为理解不同资金来源对评估编程语言很重要。

• r_singh：提到一个成功的OSS项目（mkdocs material by squidfunk）每月获得1.8万美元的资助，作为通过OSS获得收入的例子。

• sosodev：建议结合社交媒体建立个人品牌，认为拥有忠实观众的人可以通过各种方式舒适地生活。

• irf1：正在开发一个开源平台（Algora.io）来简化OSS的赏金、资助和合同工作，邀请社区提供反馈。

• koreth1：通过说服公司开放大部分代码来实现OSS贡献，尽管这些项目可能不会被外界广泛使用，但对公司的透明度和长期可行性有帮助。

• xandrius：建议说服公司为使用的OSS库做出贡献，或者通过捐赠和赏金获得收入。对黑客松的评价不高，认为其结果常受评委个人偏好影响。

• jedberg：建议找一份允许部分时间从事OSS工作的公司职位，如果幸运的话，公司会使用并支持你的OSS项目。

• Zaskoda：提到在区块链相关的黑客松中获得高额奖金的机会，但认为获胜更多依赖于营销效果而非技术创新，且结果不一定公正。

• internet_points：通过为有需求的公司提供个人OSS项目的支持获得收入，建议开发对他人难以扩展但对自己容易操作的项目。

• hugs：认为通过捐赠获得稳定收入很困难，建议通过咨询公司、大科技公司工作、创办SaaS公司或机器人公司等方式获得收入。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于通过OSS直接获得收入的可行性，部分人认为捐赠和赏金不稳定且难以维持生计，而另一些人则提供了成功的案例。
• 通过为有相关需求的公司工作或做咨询被广泛认为是一种更可靠的收入来源。
• 黑客松被一些参与者视为获得收入的机会，但其公正性和技术性受到质疑。
• 一些讨论者强调了说服公司开放和贡献代码的可能性和益处。

Prof. Sussman's Reading List
aurellem
☉
read the blog »
Written by:
Gerald Sussman (compiled by Robert McIntyre)
Serving as a TA for Professor Sussman will get you three things: great
advice, spectacular reading recommendations, and lots of high quality
tea. I can't share the advice or the tea, but I can compile a reading
list. Some of the materials on this list represent research paths that
lead to unexplored territory. Some are textbooks that express concepts
so clearly they will change your life and make you weep for joy. I
hope that you will get something interesting out of this reading list,
wherever you are in life – there's stuff I wish I knew about in
middle school, and there are things I can't wait to read this
summer. Enjoy! (and send corrections to reading-list@aurellem.org!)
–Robert McIntyre
1
Some
Real
High school Reading
A First Course in General Relativity
, by Bernard F Schultz
ISBN: 9780521277037
Readable, not too heavy.
Minimal dependencies
You can just go through it slowly and understand at each step.
Space and Time in Special Relativity
, by
David Mermin
ISBN: 0881334200
HIGHLY accessible.
This will change your life.
You will understand special relativity!
The Feynman Lectures on Physics
Highly understandable
Just go there and learn something already!
Society of Mind
, by
Marvin Minsky
A trove of wonderful ideas!
Quantum Computing since Democritus
, by
Scott Aaronson
Everything you might want to know about computing with QM, with
a philosophical outlook.
Bible, Talmud, Koran
Read them whether or not you believe them!
Be sure to read between the lines, and you can discover what
people were actually thinking back then.
Very interesting documents!
Bava Metzia 59b
is an interesting story!
2
Representative Student Theses
These are students where I played a large role in their
education. Many of them represent compelling research directions
that desperately need to be extended by the next generation of
researchers! As Minsky says, if you want to do something really new,
go back to points in the past where there was a neat idea that never
really caught on, and follow the path of that idea to see where it
leads. A comprehensive list of all my student's works can be found
at my
homepage
.
–Prof. Sussman
In particular, here's two great ideas that seem extremely promising
and have NOT been properly explored! You could be the first person
to get them working!
Using chaos to get unlimited measurement precision!
In chaotic systems, states that are near to each other at one
point in time become exponentially farther apart from each other
as the system evolves in time. Therefore, you might be able to
attain arbitrary precision by waiting for the system to evolve,
and then determining what initial state must have led to the
later state.
Two notable papers:
A Global Approach to Parameter Estimation of Chaotic Dynamical
Systems
, by
Athanassios G. Siapas
, 1992.
Parameter Estimation in Chaotic Systems
, by Elmer Hung, 1995.
No one put enough effort into seeing if it really worked.
Seems to allow for almost unlimited precision in measurement.
Initial results look very promising, with a
13 order of
magnitude
improvement in measurement precision in a simple
experiment.
You will win the Nobel Prize if you can get it to work, because
you will revolutionize the way we do measurements. In
particular, you could measure the Gravitational Constant with
unprecedented accuracy.
Towards Intelligent Structures: Active Control of Buckling
By
Andrew A. Berlin
, 1994
Achieves a 10 fold increase in strength by actively eliminating
vibrational modes.
Such a good idea; It's cool, short – great!
Better quality, color version of the thesis
here
.
No one's followed up on it!
In historical order:
A System for Representing and Using Real-World Knowledge
By
Scott Elliot Fahlman
, 1977
Basically the reason that the Connection Machine was later
invented.
The Connection Machine
By
Danny Hillis
, 1981
Beautiful thesis, though it doesn't tell you anything you can
really
do
today.
A Circuit Grammar For Operational Amplifier Design
By Andrew Ressler, 1984
If you're an Electrical Engineering person.
ONTIC: A Knowledge Representation System for Mathematics
By
David A. McAllester
, 1987
Very hard, very deep.
You will need to know a lot of Math.
KAM: Automatic Planning and Interpretation of Numerical
Experiments Using Geometrical Methods
By Kenneth Man-Kam Yip, 1989
Coolest PhD thesis ever!
Solve problems using graphs.
So cool!
Botanical Computing: A Developmental Approach to Generating
Interconnect Topologies on an Amorphous Computer
By
Daniel Coore
, 1999
Interesting to programmers especially.
Programmable Self-Assembly: Constructing Global Shape using
Biologically-inspired Local Interactions and Origami Mathematics
By
Radhika Nagpal
, 2001
Also Interesting to programmers.
Cellular Computation and Communications using Engineered Genetic
Regulatory Networks
By
Ron Weiss
, 2001

data.title: Watts Should Replace MAh as Essential Spec for Mobile Devices
data.author: m463
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了为何瓦特（watt）是电池供电设备中最关键的规格指标。作者认为，与毫安时（mAh）和兆赫兹（MHz）相比，瓦特能够更准确地反映设备的实际性能。瓦特可以衡量设备的电池提供的能量、处理器的功耗以及散热能力，从而帮助用户了解设备的续航时间和运行效率。例如，Steam Deck掌上游戏机的功耗直接影响其电池续航时间。然而，制造商往往不情愿直接提供瓦特数，而是使用其他看似更吸引人的规格来宣传产品。文章呼吁消费者关注瓦特这一指标，以便更好地理解设备的实际性能和电池寿命。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对能量（energy）和功率（power）概念的混淆以及电池参数的正确标注方式。

不同观点：
• [perilunar] 认为原文混淆了能量和功率的概念，并建议电池应标明总能量（如Wh或J）以及最大功率输出（W）。具体来说，他认为能量是做功的总量，而功率是做功的速度。他指出，文章的错误在于没有清晰区分这两个概念。

• [johndoe0815] 对原文中关于瓦特（功率单位）的解释表示不满，但未详细展开具体的技术错误，仅表达了对功率概念解释不当的不满。

• [JohnFen] 表示对能量和功率混淆问题早已不满，支持[perilunar]对文章错误的批评，但没有提出新的论据或建议。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于文章对能量和功率的错误混用。具体来说，[perilunar]明确指出能量是总量（如Wh），而功率是单位时间的能量（如W），因此电池的标注应明确区分这两者。

• 讨论中还隐含了对消费者知情权的关注，即电池性能应通过明确的、不混淆的参数来标注，以便消费者能够准确理解产品的性能表现。

• 尽管[johndoe0815]和[JohnFen]都表达了不满，但他们的评论主要是支持[perilunar]的观点，并未提出新的解决方案或额外论据。

Forget mAh, and stop sweating megahertz. The watt reigns supreme, if only companies would share it with us.

Part Of
Spec-tacular week
see all
Sean Hollister
is a senior editor and founding member of The Verge who covers gadgets, games, and toys. He spent 15 years editing the likes of CNET, Gizmodo, and Engadget.
Every time I see “mAh” on a consumer product, I cringe. Megahertz are starting to bruise, too. That’s because the most critical components of portable gadgets — batteries and processors — should really be measured in watts: it’s the one common spec that gives you a real idea of what your device can do.
With watts, you can tell how much literal power is under the hood — how much energy is provided by your battery and how much is coursing through your chip. Watts determine whether there’s enough cooling to let that processor run free, instead of overheating and throttling prematurely. Watts can even tell you how much battery life you have left, based on the watt-hours (Wh) of battery remaining and the wattage at which your device is draining.
You can do it all with elementary school math — so why aren’t watts everywhere? Consumers are regularly exposed to wattage measurements when buying light bulbs or reading their power bills. But many gadget manufacturers insist on measuring their batteries in milliamp-hours and their chip speed in megahertz or gigahertz, neither of which are a good measure of a device’s true power.
The Steam Deck gaming handheld is my go-to example of how handy watts can be. With a 15-watt maximum processor wattage and up to 9 watts of overhead for other components, a strenuous game drains its 49Wh battery in roughly two hours flat. My eight-year-old can do that math: 15 plus 9 is 24, and 24 times 2 is 48. You can fit two hour-long 24-watt sessions into 48Wh, and because you have 49Wh, you’re almost sure to get it.
With the least strenuous games, I’ll sometimes see my Steam Deck draining the battery at a speed of just 6 watts — which means I can get eight hours of gameplay because 6 watts times 8 hours is 48Wh, with 1Wh remaining in the 49Wh battery.
The Steam Deck OLED.
Photo: Vjeran Pavic / The Verge
At its most basic, the watt is a measure of work. It’s the amount of energy it takes to
do
something at a particular
speed
, whether it’s heating up food in your 1,000-watt microwave or providing the 2-3 watts a smartphone needs while you’re browsing websites on its screen. It’s also specifically a measure of electricity — watts are volts times amps — and a measure of battery capacity, like my Steam Deck example above. (My colleague Thomas Ricker can also
help you calculate watt-hours for off-grid energy storage and home backup
.)
Perhaps most intriguingly, watts are used as a roundabout measure of heat. If you’ve ever seen a computer processor with a certain TDP, or thermal design power, measured in watts, that’s the amount of
cooling
required to run that chip at its normal speed. A chip is only as fast as it can be cooled, which is why watts are more important than megahertz.
Today’s laptops have long broken the 5GHz barrier, meaning their chips can theoretically do work five billion times per second.
Phone chips are coming close, too
. But in small and constrained battery-powered devices, they can only maintain those speeds briefly before they overheat. It’s why a MacBook Pro with a fan has better sustained performance than a MacBook Air without one,
even if they both have the exact same chip
. It’s part of why a “15-watt” processor will generally feel slower than a “28-watt” one, even if both can hit 5GHz. More power and more cooling means you’re not just a sprinter; you can go the distance.
Unfortunately, manufacturers aren’t always fond of sharing watts with us. They’d prefer to quote bigger, more impressive-sounding numbers instead, advertising a power bank or phone with a “5,000mAh battery” rather than a 19.4Wh pack. You can
convert mAh to Wh
, but only if you know the device’s voltage, which is another spec that’s often obscured. Some chip makers even hide the wattage of their chips so you won’t know you’re using a weaker version, such as an 80-watt Nvidia RTX 4080 laptop graphics chip instead of a 150-watt one, though admittedly more power
doesn’t always make a big difference
.
James Watt left behind a legacy of pushing confusing specs
Manufacturers also prefer to share what percentage of your battery is remaining rather than an actually useful number like the watt. They prefer to let you choose vague power modes like “performance,” “balanced,” and “battery saver,” instead of using the sm
43561591.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了为何瓦特（watt）是电池供电设备中最关键的规格指标。作者认为，与毫安时（mAh）和兆赫兹（MHz）相比，瓦特能够更准确地反映设备的实际性能。瓦特可以衡量设备的电池提供的能量、处理器的功耗以及散热能力，从而帮助用户了解设备的续航时间和运行效率。例如，Steam Deck掌上游戏机的功耗直接影响其电池续航时间。然而，制造商往往不情愿直接提供瓦特数，而是使用其他看似更吸引人的规格来宣传产品。文章呼吁消费者关注瓦特这一指标，以便更好地理解设备的实际性能和电池寿命。

主要讨论点：对能量（energy）和功率（power）概念的混淆以及电池参数的正确标注方式。

不同观点：
• [perilunar] 认为原文混淆了能量和功率的概念，并建议电池应标明总能量（如Wh或J）以及最大功率输出（W）。具体来说，他认为能量是做功的总量，而功率是做功的速度。他指出，文章的错误在于没有清晰区分这两个概念。

• [johndoe0815] 对原文中关于瓦特（功率单位）的解释表示不满，但未详细展开具体的技术错误，仅表达了对功率概念解释不当的不满。

• [JohnFen] 表示对能量和功率混淆问题早已不满，支持[perilunar]对文章错误的批评，但没有提出新的论据或建议。

• 讨论中还隐含了对消费者知情权的关注，即电池性能应通过明确的、不混淆的参数来标注，以便消费者能够准确理解产品的性能表现。

data.title: The reality of working in tech: We're not hired to write code (2023)
data.author: foxfired
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了一位开发人员在公司中经历的职业变迁和感悟。他的一位前同事因不满新政策而离职，这位同事曾是公司唯一的 .Net 开发人员，负责多个关键网站。同事离开后，系统出现问题，但团队无人能立即解决，最终由一名墨西哥的QA人员通过重启服务器解决了问题，并因此获得晋升。作者回顾自己的经历，尽管他曾是团队中的JavaScript专家，但随着技术发展和新工具的引入，他的工作逐渐被替代。他意识到在快速变化的科技行业中，公司更注重产品和功能的交付，而非个人的编码能力。通过担任顾问，他进一步理解到，向客户和管理层展示可见的成果比单纯的编码工作更受重视。最终，他反思是否应该继续专注于编写代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：程序员的角色和价值，特别是在代码编写与其他工作任务之间的关系，以及薪酬和职业定位问题。

不同观点：
• **[mcv]** 认为程序员，尤其是高级程序员，在荷兰的薪酬不如经理、产品负责人、架构师，甚至Scrum master。他分享了自己从自由职业者转为正式员工后收入下降的经历，并指出公司内部规定限制了程序员获得更高的薪酬，尽管他们解决了复杂的非代码相关问题。

• **[Willingham]** 指出，有大约10%的开发者是系统开发者，他们的工作核心是代码本身，特别是在操作系统、编译器、数据库内核等领域。在这些岗位上，代码的正确性、稳定性和兼容性是首要的，因此新旧技术交替的频率较低。

• **[don-code]** 分享了与一位擅长写代码的同事的经历，并指出写代码虽然是解决问题的途径之一，但不总是最好的方式。他鼓励减少代码编写量，更多地考虑代码编写的背景和目的。

• **[lijok]** 认为开发者的主要任务是实现商业目标，代码编写只是其中一种手段。最好的开发者是那些能够说服经理使用简单工具（如WordPress）来实现商业目标的人。

• **[arealaccount]** 以赛车手作比喻，认为开发者被雇佣的目的不是写代码，而是解决问题和达成业务目标，尽管这一点可能显得有些学究气。

• **[MathMonkeyMan]** 提到其工作主要是弄清楚该做什么，修改代码，并与其他人沟通原因。编写新代码或删除不需要的代码是有趣的部分，但并非总是可行。

• **[vkaku]** 认为程序员的价值不仅在于解决问题，还在于执行。如果程序员不专注于执行而陷入官僚主义，公司可能会破产。

• **[prescriptivist]** 指出，随着LLM（大型语言模型）的兴起，现代开发者的工作更多是管理代码而非编写代码。尽管LLM可以大幅提高代码生成速度，但也带来了质量和兼容性问题。

• **[dev_mike12]** 强调了合同工作中明确沟通和范围定义的重要性，并指出与信任的客户合作能带来更好的咨询体验。

• **[em-bee]** 讨论了由于缺乏对新技术的经验而无法参与新功能实现的问题，质疑这是否是因为个人能力不足或公司内部的 dysfunction。

• **[WalterBright]** 简单指出，程序员被雇佣的目的是为公司赚钱。

• **[MPSimmons]** 认为公司雇佣程序员的目的不是写代码，而是通过软件开发实现商业目标。代码编写是手段而非目的，最弱的开发者也需具备基本的胜任能力。

• **[xnx]** 直言代码是一种负债，公司目标是以最少的代码、员工和成本解决问题。

• **[yawnxyz]** 质疑如果代码不重要，为什么LeetCode仍然是进入大公司的必要条件。

• **[94b45eb4]** 回顾了早期的观点，即程序员的工作是解决问题，而非单纯写代码。他指出当今许多初级开发者过于关注代码的表面和流行框架，而忽视了问题的本质和解决方案的权衡。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于程序员是否应专注于代码编写，还是应更广泛地参与问题解决和商业目标实现。
- 薪酬问题也是讨论的核心，特别是高级程序员与其他角色之间的薪酬差异。
- LLM和现代工具对开发者角色的影响引发了对代码质量和生成速度的讨论。

43563533.article_content:
"So, is everyone losing their minds yet?"
My ex-coworker asked me over yahoo messenger. He quit after getting enraged by new work policies that specifically targeted him. I looked up from my screen, and saw that the team of developers who used to work alongside my ex-coworker were now silently working on their respective machines in the row next to me. His old monitor had been taken away. His tower was sitting on the now open office desk, collecting its first coat of dust.
"Yes. It's complete chaos." I replied. Well, I lied. It wasn't chaos. They weren't happy either. The reality was that his old team was indifferent. They missed him of course, he was a great guy. I missed him, he was a true friend in this chaotic world of technology. But the fact that he was the only .Net developer in the entire company went unnoticed.
By himself, he maintained multiple money making websites. They all ran on a brittle .Net infrastructure. He knew all there was to know about them, and would respond in seconds whenever they experienced an issue. There was no realistic way to replace my ex-coworker, the .Net developer, and there were no plans in place to address this issue. He was hired to write code, so the best way to get back at a company who didn't value him, was to stop writing code. So he quit.
"lol the website is down," he wrote to me the next day. I checked and he was right, the website was down. I looked in the next row and it was complete silence. A whole hour passed and I was getting nervous. Not a single person in his old team was talking about it. I sent a message to one of them. "Hey I think your website is down."
"Oh, you are right." She answered. "I'll investigate."
After lunch, The QA guy in Mexico sent me a message on AIM, asking if I knew the credentials to the server. I shared the credentials. Then he said "Is SSH disabled on this server? It just times out."
"It's a windows server," I answered. "You have to use RDP to connect."
"Oh boy! I never used a Windows server before."
I helped him access the server and went on my way. Before the day was over, the website was back up. He was later promoted and became the new .Net guy. The QA guy in Mexico resolved the issue by simply restarting the machine.
My old friend, once a crucial part of the organization, was no longer needed. They built a new UI written in PHP and plugged the same database. Not only was he replaced, but now his position had been phased out. .Net was no longer a thing in the company. The promoted employee in Mexico was soon let go.
I thought I had been hired for my ability to write code as well. I posed as the JavaScript guru. Everyone consulted with me before deploying any code. In 2011, you needed an expert to guarantee your code would run on the plethora of broken browsers. We wouldn't dream of the tools available today. I was that expert. Yet when I left, my team moved on.
Despite my skills as a JavaScript developer, my position had been gradually diluted into a larger team of developers who were capable of handling the job just fine.
I was once proud of my self-developed methods for testing my scripts across various browsers and effectively implementing feature detection. However, the company eventually switched to using jQuery instead of my custom-built methods. Similarly, my custom tools were replaced with a third-party vendor's offering. While I was previously the go-to person for building new features, I was unable to contribute to the implementation of Angular due to my lack of experience with it.
I was proudest of an A/B testing suite I built for the company. It rivaled Google's Web Optimizer, and it was customizable. It ran both on the server side and the client side. It was the result of years of internal feedback and fine tuning. I even made a fun little logo for it. One day, a new manager came in and said we should use VWO as an alternative to Google's. And that was it. My work was tossed away without a second thought.
If they had hired me to write code, or if my old friend was hired to maintain what was exotic code, then why was it so easy to discard it?
I later realized that in the fast-paced tech industry, companies prioritize delivering products and features above all else. Managers are responsible for delivering results to higher-ups. As such, it is crucial for developers to work on building and maintaining the company's products and features, regardless of their coding specializations.
My experiences as a consultant further highlighted the importance of delivering visual results to clients and stakeholders. I often spent night and day fixing bugs and performance issues only for the company to ask me if I did any work. But when I produced "A Subscription Model" or "An Architecture" or "A build system" these were highly praised. Even though they came in as a PowerPoint instead of working code. They would hand it over to a team to write the code later, if ever.

data.title: I maintain a 17 year old ThinkPad
data.author: Fred34
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了为何作者仍然使用一台17年前的Thinkpad笔记本电脑，并通过Nassim Nicholas Taleb的"反脆弱"理论和Lindy效应解释其原因。旧款Thinkpad因其模块化设计、可更换组件（如电池、内存、存储等）以及坚固的做工，展现出高度的耐用性和" robustness"（坚固性）。这种设计允许用户轻松维修和升级设备，延长其使用寿命。相比之下，现代MacBook尽管性能强大，但其设计更为" fragile"（脆弱）。由于组件多为焊接在主板上，且使用专有配件，维修困难，单一组件损坏可能导致整个设备无法使用。此外，MacBook的软件支持有限，一旦停止更新，设备可能迅速过时。因此，作者认为旧Thinkpad凭借其开放性和可修复性，展现出更强的生命力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ThinkPad和Framework笔记本的比较与可修复性讨论

不同观点：
• CursedSilicon认为Framework笔记本在可修复性和组件更换方面表现出色，尤其在长期拥有成本上可能更低。然而，作为小众制造商，其入门门槛较高，与ThinkPad这样在二手市场非常成功的机型相比，Framework还难以达到同样的成功水平。
• quailfarmer则支持硬件的紧密整合，认为这是提高可靠性、降低成本和提升性能的必要手段。虽然可更换组件的设计很巧妙，但并非必要功能，且紧密整合的设计并不一定牺牲质量。
• inatreecrown2和tyushk表达了对旧款ThinkPad设计（如尺寸、可修复性、接口和键盘）的喜爱，并希望有一款具备现代内部硬件的类似设计的新机型。
• interroboink指出，旧硬件在操作系统更新后可能面临支持问题，导致无法运行新软件，进而限制使用场景。
• ivraatiems和ajxs分享了使用旧ThinkPad（如T580、x220）的经验，强调了其耐用性和在Linux系统下的出色表现。
• ed_mercer和justmarc欣赏旧ThinkPad的经典设计和坚固性，并认为使用Linux等开源系统可以延长这些机器的使用寿命。
• dpedu提供了关于MacBook电池更换的实际经验，指出并非所有型号都难以维修。
• markus_zhang和zh3分享了他们使用T470S和T420等机型的经验，强调了这些机型的实用性和在Linux系统下的良好表现，但也提到了图形驱动等问题。
• kombine介绍了自己使用ThinkPad T14s Gen3 AMD的经验，认为其在性价比和Linux兼容性上表现出色。
• frfl提出了寻找耐用ThinkPad电池的困难，对市场上电池质量表示担忧。

补充讨论：
• 关于ThinkPad在二手市场的成功，CursedSilicon提到其广泛的市场存量和长久以来的商业使用，使其在二手市场非常成功。
• 关于操作系统支持，interroboink指出旧硬件在运行新操作系统时可能会遇到支持问题，限制其使用新软件的能力。
• 关于电池寿命和更换，frfl和dpedu提到寻找高质量电池和更换电池的实际困难。

争议焦点：

43564111.article_content:
Why I Maintain a 17 Year Old Thinkpad
Published on: April 1, 2025
If a book has been in print for forty years, I can expect it to be in print for another forty years. But, and that is the main difference, if it survives another decade, then it will be expected to be in print another fifty years. This, simply, as a rule, tells you why things that have been around for a long time are not "aging" like persons, but "aging" in reverse. Every year that passes without extinction doubles the additional life expectancy. This is an indicator of some robustness. The robustness of an item is proportional to its life
― Nassim Nicholas Taleb, Antifragile
Nassim Nicholas Taleb contrasts
fragile
systems—those that suffer serious harm under volatility—with
robust
systems that can endure stress with minimal damage. He extends this concept with
antifragile
systems, which can actually benefit from disorder, but we’ll focus here on the divide between fragile and robust.
Taleb also introduces the
Lindy Effect
as an idea about longevity: if something non-perishable has been around for a long time, that track record suggests it’s likely to keep going. We’ll see how this relates to two laptops—one from 2008, the other from 2021.
Old Thinkpads: Modular, Robust Survivors
IBM and early Lenovo Thinkpads showcases a design built for longevity. Despite their age, these business-class laptop are still serviceable and useful for web browsing, ‘office work’, and light coding. These machine are too slow to handle tasks like video editing or gaming, but they remain consistent in handling everyday tasks without failing under normal wear and tear.
One of the main reasons that old Thinkpads stand out is their
design philosophy
. They are made with swappable components with the intention of user upgradeability. The battery, RAM, storage drive, keyboard, and even the CPU can be easily replaced. I can open the bottom of my T400 with a regular screwdriver and clean the fan. A battery swap is trivial thanks to a removable pack. No single failure is catastrophic because there’s a straightforward path to replacement or repair.
The
build quality
greatly contributes to old Thinkpads robustness. They are made with a sturdy chassis with plastic and magnesium alloy elements, giving it a solid feel. The design absorbs bumps and small impacts without major issues. They can easily take accidental knocks and remain fully operational.
Old Thinkpads benefits from an
open ecosystem
. They uses standard PC architecture (x86), so installing various operating systems is easy. On the hardware side, replacement parts are widely available on the secondary market. This broad compatibility keeps the machine relevant long past its original release date. By Taleb’s Lindy Effect, the fact that my T400 can still work well after so many years suggests
it’s likely to remain functional as people have already figured out the ways to significantly extend its lifespan
.
All these factors show how the my Thinkpad is
robust
: it resists sudden failures, and when problems do arise, their are documented way to fit it. Old beat up Thinkpads are Lindy.
Modern MacBooks: High Performance, But Fragile
My MacBook offers exceptional speed and efficiency an order of magnitude more than my Thinkpad. It handles tasks—like video editing or running large LLM’s without breaking a sweat. Under ideal conditions, it’s reliable and powerful.
However, from a Talebian perspective, my MacBook’s design is
fragile
. Most components of the laptop are soldered onto the logic board. If the SSD or RAM fails, there’s no simple replacement option. A single failure in a component of my MacBook can render the entire laptop unusable. The tightly integrated design of modern Apple hardware increases the stakes of any malfunction.
The
repairability
of Apple products is extremely limited. Apple uses proprietary screws and adhesives, and parts are incompatible with third-party replacements. A battery replacement (usually one of the first things that fails in mobile electronics) involves carefully prying out a glued component. Routine maintenance tasks that are straightforward on the Thinkpad can require specialized tools and authorized service for the MacBook. This lack of modularity means the system can easily become bricked from hardware fails from component parts.
Another aspect contributing to the fragility of MacBooks is Apple’s
software control
. Apple’s software updates and security updates to macOS essentially determines how long the MacBook remains safe to use. Once Apple ends official support for a machine the user has to buy a new MacBook or use an increasingly compromised system. Apple hardware uses an arm architecture that cannot ‘dual boot’ Windows or Linux easily. Once macOS support dies for a modern MacBook it becomes obsolete.
While my MacBook is great to use, the machine has a lifespan built into its OS support and cannot recover easily from physical damage. MacBooks are not modular, completely propriet
43564111.article_summary: 本文讨论了为何作者仍然使用一台17年前的Thinkpad笔记本电脑，并通过Nassim Nicholas Taleb的"反脆弱"理论和Lindy效应解释其原因。旧款Thinkpad因其模块化设计、可更换组件（如电池、内存、存储等）以及坚固的做工，展现出高度的耐用性和" robustness"（坚固性）。这种设计允许用户轻松维修和升级设备，延长其使用寿命。相比之下，现代MacBook尽管性能强大，但其设计更为" fragile"（脆弱）。由于组件多为焊接在主板上，且使用专有配件，维修困难，单一组件损坏可能导致整个设备无法使用。此外，MacBook的软件支持有限，一旦停止更新，设备可能迅速过时。因此，作者认为旧Thinkpad凭借其开放性和可修复性，展现出更强的生命力。

data.title: Search could be so much better. And I don't mean chatbots with web access
data.author: mfkhalil
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种新型搜索引擎MatterRank，其核心特点是让用户能够控制搜索结果的排序，而不仅仅是让算法猜测用户的需求。传统的搜索引擎通过关键词、链接和各种信号来猜测用户意图，而MatterRank允许用户用自己的语言描述如何排序结果，提供更个性化和精准的搜索体验。这不是一个简单的聊天机器人或智能自动补全工具，而是一种全新的搜索方式，让用户决定什么最重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：搜索引擎的使用体验和功能改进

不同观点：
• maximumgeek：认为当前的搜索体验较差，广告多且搜索结果不准确，尤其提到对Quora答案的不满，并批评帖子内容毫无价值，缺乏具体指导。
• renegat0x0：提出使用SQLite数据库进行搜索的方案，强调搜索相关性与反垃圾信息的重要性，但承认这一任务的复杂性。
• AymanJabr：反对强制注册和创建搜索引擎的步骤，希望搜索应用能够直接使用，无需额外操作，除非用户自己选择。
• SteveDavis88：希望搜索引擎能精确返回包含指定关键词的结果，对Google的现有功能表示不满。
• mfkhalil：支持在搜索中加入定性特征，如内容作者、特定引用等，认为这样能提高搜索精度，传统搜索引擎无法满足这种需求。
• danpalmer：不认同搜索引擎假设用户不知道自己想要什么，认为搜索中的垃圾信息问题确实存在，但不应过度解读为用户需求不明。

• BrenBarn：指出不光是搜索引擎，很多现代技术都倾向于告诉用户该做什么，而非让用户自主选择。
• eternauta3k：质疑在每个搜索结果上运行LLM的成本是否过高。

• TekMol：强烈反对需要注册账户才能使用搜索引擎的做法。

补充讨论：
• 搜索引擎广告过多及如何有效过滤广告是用户普遍关注的问题。
• 用户对搜索结果的精确度及相关性有较高要求，希望减少不相关信息。
• 使用LLM进行搜索排名的速度和成本问题引起讨论，部分用户对其效率表示担忧。

43563915.article_content:
Search could be so much better
And I don't mean chatbots with access to a search engine.
Search is suffering from a quiet, unfortunate assumption. One that made the internet accessible to billions—but made it much less personal than it could be.
It assumes we don't know what we want.
This isn't search engines' fault. For decades, the only way we could communicate what we wanted was through a little search box.
So they did their best. They built systems to guess what we meant—ranking pages based on overlapping words, backlinks, reputation, and a hundred other signals. The best version of that became PageRank. And it was so good, it powered one of the most valuable companies in history.
But then computers learned how to understand language.
Now, we can do something new: we can tell search engines not just what we want, but
how we want it ranked
.
MatterRank is the first search engine where you control the ranking—using your own words.
This isn't a chatbot that summarizes results. And it's not just smarter autocomplete.
It's a new kind of search engine—one that lets you decide what matters most.
Let me know what you uncover. My email's below.
—Moe Khalil
Founder of MatterRank
moe@matterrank.ai
Try it now!
...or read more about how it works
→

data.title: Search-R1: Training LLMs to Reason and Leverage Search Engines with RL
data.author: jonbaer
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为Search-R1的模型，它通过强化学习（RL）训练大型语言模型（LLM）在推理过程中自主生成搜索查询并与搜索引擎互动。与仅在推理阶段提示LLM使用搜索引擎不同，Search-R1在多轮搜索交互中优化LLM的表现，利用检索到的标记屏蔽实现稳定的RL训练和基于结果的奖励函数。实验表明，Search-R1在多个问答数据集上的性能比强基准模型提高了10%到26%。本文还探讨了RL优化方法、LLM选择及响应长度对检索增强推理的影响，并提供了代码和模型检查点。

Abstract:
Efficiently acquiring external knowledge and up-to-date information is essential for effective reasoning and text generation in large language models (LLMs). Prompting advanced LLMs with reasoning capabilities during inference to use search engines is not optimal, since the LLM does not learn how to optimally interact with the search engine. This paper introduces Search-R1, an extension of the DeepSeek-R1 model where the LLM learns -- solely through reinforcement learning (RL) -- to autonomously generate (multiple) search queries during step-by-step reasoning with real-time retrieval. Search-R1 optimizes LLM rollouts with multi-turn search interactions, leveraging retrieved token masking for stable RL training and a simple outcome-based reward function. Experiments on seven question-answering datasets show that Search-R1 improves performance by 26% (Qwen2.5-7B), 21% (Qwen2.5-3B), and 10% (LLaMA3.2-3B) over strong baselines. This paper further provides empirical insights into RL optimization methods, LLM choices, and response length dynamics in retrieval-augmented reasoning. 43563265.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为Search-R1的模型，它通过强化学习（RL）训练大型语言模型（LLM）在推理过程中自主生成搜索查询并与搜索引擎互动。与仅在推理阶段提示LLM使用搜索引擎不同，Search-R1在多轮搜索交互中优化LLM的表现，利用检索到的标记屏蔽实现稳定的RL训练和基于结果的奖励函数。实验表明，Search-R1在多个问答数据集上的性能比强基准模型提高了10%到26%。本文还探讨了RL优化方法、LLM选择及响应长度对检索增强推理的影响，并提供了代码和模型检查点。
43563265.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI研究在开放环境下的合作与发展，特别是DeepSeek模型的发布及其方法论，以及该模型在不同应用场景中的技术细节和潜在问题。

不同观点：
• [perbu] 认为AI研究的公开性促进了技术进步，并举例说明DeepSeek公开了其模型和方法，使得其他研究机构如伊利诺伊大学能够在其基础上进行进一步的研究。他还表达了对OpenAI初期愿景的感慨，希望AI研究能够造福人类。

• [deepsquirrelnet] 对DeepSeek模型表示赞赏，并提到自己有一个类似的模型正在训练中，计划发布完整的蒸馏数据集，提供了一个链接供其他人查看。

• [0xlogk] 关注DeepSeek模型使用的搜索语料库及其未来扩展计划，特别是提到从Wikipedia到Google和Bing API的扩展，并提出持续强化学习更新的必要性以处理不断变化的搜索语料库。

• [DeathArrow] 请求用简单易懂的方式解释强化学习如何与基于Transformer的架构结合使用，显示出对技术细节的兴趣和可能的困惑。

• [sachinaag] 对Perplexity是否使用与DeepSeek类似的方法表示好奇，或者认为Perplexity可能采用完全不同的方法。

补充讨论：

• 评论中涉及对强化学习和Transformer架构结合的兴趣，以及对不同模型和方法之间比较的思考。
• 讨论中还提到了具体的数据集和模型训练进度，显示出开放科学和合作在AI研究中的重要性。

data.title: Tech companies are telling immigrant employees on visas not to leave the U.S.
data.author: prtaylor
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HN（Hacker News）上关于H1B签证及相关问题的讨论，尤其是对美国当前形势变化的看法和签证政策的争议。

不同观点：
• [Teever] 认为HN上有关某些敏感话题（如签证和法律问题）的讨论较少，可能是因为人们害怕讨论或不了解情况。他指出，美国的形势正在迅速变化，人们将无法永远忽视这些问题。

• [brcmthrowaway] 建议持有H1B签证的人在入境美国时使用一次性手机（burner phone），认为这样可以避免麻烦，暗示可能有监控或信息泄露的风险。

• [zombiwoof] 指出其他国家也对美国人采取类似的签证限制措施，认为美国的H1B签证政策早就应该调整，因为没有其他国家像美国一样大量发放H1B签证。

• [Yeul] 提到目前获得中国签证比以往任何时候都更加顺畅，并且中国人对他的欧元表示欢迎，暗示其他国家的签证政策可能比美国更友好或更简单。

• [xqcgrek2] 简短地评论，提到廉价劳动力不应离开，似乎是在讨论H1B签证持有者对美国企业的价值。

• [sjtgraham] 批评有关H1B的标题不准确，强调H1B签证本质上是非移民签证，持有人是临时工而非移民，认为这种误解或误导性的标题不合适。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是H1B签证的性质和其持有者是否应被视为移民。这反映了公众对签证政策的不同理解和潜在误解。
• 另一个值得注意的点是不同国家之间签证政策的比较，尤其是美国与其他国家在签证发放方面的差异，以及这些差异对个人和企业的影响。
• 讨论中还涉及对当前美国形势变化的担忧，以及这些变化可能对签证持有者产生的影响。

data.author: whoishiring
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同公司和岗位的招聘信息及要求

不同观点：
• [skeeter2020] 强调Absorb LMS正在寻找一位有经验的软件开发团队领导，特别是能够领导AI/ML团队的人。该岗位需要有Python开发经验，并且团队分布在不同地点，实行远程工作模式。
• [amacneil] 介绍了Foxglove的招聘岗位，包括Staff Product Designer、Full Stack Product Engineer等，公司主要为机器人开发者提供可观察性平台，岗位要求涉及WebGL、Wasm、TypeScript等技术。
• [allenjhyang] 提到了Liminary正在招聘创始工程团队的最后两名成员，岗位包括Product Engineer - Frontend和AI Engineer，公司目标是为知识工作者构建认知伴侣。
• [getgalaxy] 宣传了Galaxy正在构建的SQL查询工具，招聘包括Founding ML Engineer、Front End Visualization Engineer等职位，目标是取代旧有的数据库工具。
• [zecto] 分享了Black Canyon Consulting在NCBI的招聘信息，岗位包括Platform Systems Engineers，强调了对Linux、K8s、Kafka等技术的需求以及对政府技术现代化的贡献。
• [ridiculous_fish] 介绍了Oklo的招聘信息，公司正在开发新一代核反应堆，招聘岗位包括Software Engineer和Software Quality Assurance Engineer，工作地点可以选择远程或实体办公室。
• [umutisik] 提到了Incept AI的招聘，公司专注于解决语音AI的最后一公里问题，招聘包括Software Engineers和Deep Learning Scientists，岗位要求有深度学习和神经网络的经验。
• [jamesjyu] 分享了Sudowrite的招聘信息，公司正在开发AI写作工具，强调团队的低 Drama 和高效率，招聘AI Engineer，要求对文学有热爱。
• [tbcj] 介绍了Bloomberg的软件工程师招聘信息，岗位包括基础设施软件工程师，工作地点在纽约和伦敦，强调了对高性能分布式系统的开发。
• [gottabecreative] 分享了Deutsche Börse在布拉格的招聘信息，岗位是Kotlin Software Engineer，公司正在开发下一代能源交易平台，技术栈包括Kotlin Flow、WebSockets、gRPC等。
• [azaydak] 提到了Yotta Navigation的招聘信息，招聘Lead Front End React Developer，要求有Mapbox或类似经验，岗位负责开发前端Web应用。
• [kevinqi] 分享了Gridmatic的招聘信息，公司利用ML和天气数据预测能源价格，招聘Senior fullstack software engineer和Senior backend software engineer，技术栈包括React/Nextjs、Kubernetes、GCP等。
• [jrudin] 介绍了Clad的招聘信息，公司为基础设施建设提供管理软件，招聘Full Stack Software Engineer，技术栈包括TypeScript和Remix。
• [madiganf] 分享了Fathom的招聘信息，公司开发AI Notetaker工具，招聘包括Rails+TypeScript和Go开发工程师，强调团队的高效协作和快速出货。

补充讨论：
• 多个公司（如[skeeter2020]、[amacneil]、[allenjhyang]）都提到了远程工作模式，反映了疫情后远程工作的普及。
• 技术要求多样化，包括Python、TypeScript、React、Kotlin、Go等，反映了不同公司对技术栈的偏好和需求。
• 一些公司（如[jamesjyu]、[tbcj]）强调了团队文化和低 Drama，反映了招聘中对团队协作和员工文化的重视。
• 多个公司（如[getgalaxy]、[zecto]、[kevinqi]）提到了对政府或大型机构的技术支持和贡献，反映了技术公司在社会基础设施现代化中的角色。

争议焦点：
• 不同公司对远程工作和实体办公室的偏好有所不同，可能引发对工作模式的讨论和争议。
• 一些岗位要求高度专业化的技术经验（如[umutisik]的深度学习要求），可能引发对招聘门槛和多样性的讨论。

data.title: Why I don't discuss politics with friends
data.author: shw1n
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了作者为何避免与朋友讨论政治问题。主要原因有三个：首先，大多数人并非持有政治观点，而是依附于政治部落；其次，形成独立政治见解需要极高的智力和知识，而这非常困难；最后，多数人其实并不想脱离部落思维。人们往往通过验证他人是否 adherence 部落文化来提问政治问题，而非真诚探讨。政治讨论常演变为宗教般的意识形态之争，人们更愿意依附于群体信念，而非独立思考。作者认为，尽管克服部落主义是可能的，但许多人并不愿意这么做，因为他们从部落中获得了情感和社交上的满足。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：政治讨论的社会风险、个人与社会成长、政治分歧对人际关系的影响

不同观点：
• [sD4fG_9hJ] 认为政治讨论中的尊重参与和理解彼此的价值观和经历，有助于个人和社会成长。强调通过理解对方背后的价值观和经验，可以使讨论更加有成效。

• [rdegges] 提出反对意见，认为某些政治立场和决策可能对特定群体造成实际伤害，因此与持这些观点的人断绝关系是值得的。在这种情境下，没有共同基础可以讨论。

• [simpaticoder] 认为人们不愿意改变立场是因为自我反思是痛苦的，且可能不利于自身利益。提到Citizens United案后的法律系统对公众辩论的影响，使得对抗性辩论系统缺乏公正的裁判。

• [pcblues] 描述了过去几十年政治讨论的变化，从避免讨论到开放讨论，再到近年因社交媒体导致的部落主义。引用了Maria Ressa和Jon Stewart的谈话来说明这一变化。

• [JohnFen] 对“谁给你投票”的问题感到惊讶，认为这在他们的社交圈中是禁忌话题，并指出这种直接询问在社交中是不礼貌的。

• [panstromek] 认为人们的行为比他们的言论或政治立场更重要，主张关注可以实际达成共识并采取行动的领域，而不是空泛的政治辩论。

• [delichon] 否认独立思考必然导致温和立场，认为最独立的思考者往往会走向极端。

• [daft_pink] 提到会果断屏蔽在社交媒体上不断发布政治新闻或抱怨的人。

• [greybox] 用“你可以正确，或者你可以有朋友”来比喻政治讨论中选择正确立场和维护友谊之间的矛盾。

• [makeitdouble] 用宗教信仰作类比，认为每个人都有自己的界限，政治或宗教分歧超出这个界限就会导致关系的破裂。

• [mattgreenrocks] 提出未来社会将更明显地分裂为偏好现实和偏好非现实的人，非现实是由互联网等媒介构建的，与实际经验脱节。

• [protonbob] 调侃博客中的图片常被用来嘲笑 faux intellectualism 和道德优越感。

• [stretchwithme] 认为在线政治讨论不值得，因为风险高且成本效益比差，建议通过发布公开言论来影响更多人。

• [marcuschong] 描述了在其国家政治讨论变得像宗教问题一样，人们因价值观不同而感到被对立，管理家庭关系变得困难。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到政治讨论的痛苦和风险，以及因政治分歧导致的人际关系破裂。
• 强调现实与非现实之间的分裂，以及社交媒体在加剧部落主义和对抗性辩论中的角色。
• 提及Citizens United案对法律和公众辩论的影响，以及缺乏公正裁判的问题。
• 讨论了政治讨论在不同文化和社交圈中的禁忌和礼貌问题。

43559605.article_content:
Why I don't discuss politics with friends
Update: There is something poetic about this essay on tribalism getting removed from users abusing the flagging system (then restored) after hitting #3 on Hacker News  😆
March 2025
For as much as I enjoy analyzing politics[1], I'm even more against discussing it with friends. This policy arose from three patterns observed over the years:
Most people don't have political views, they have political
tribes
Developing the political reasoning skills to graduate from tribes to views is incredibly difficult
and the kicker:
Most people don't
want
to graduate from tribes to views
Often when someone asks "who did you vote for", what they're actually doing is verifying your adherence to group culture, like a congregation member asking "you believe in god, right?" loudly in church.
The insidious nature of this question comes from the false representation as earnest, intellectual discourse. Many who ask it may truly believe they’re engaging earnestly, but their responses quickly reveal an angle more akin to religious police.
Most vulnerable to this behavior are the intellectually honest + socially clueless, who engage in good faith, unaware of the pending social ambush.
Why does this happen?
I think there are two main reasons, the first being the sheer intellectual difficulty of crafting an informed political view leads people to tribalism out of convenience.
Being informed is tough
To have an informed view on any given issue, one needs to:
understand economics, game theory, philosophy, sales, business, military strategy, geopolitics, sociology, history, and more
be able to understand and empathize with the various (and often opposing) groups involved in a topic
detect and ignore their own bias
How can you prioritize limited resources with deadly consequences without understanding utilitarianism vs deontology (i.e. the trolly problem)?
Understand China-US relations without understanding communism vs capitalism, the fear of tyranny vs the threat of invasion, or how and where computer chips are made?
How military power dictates realities, economies affect happiness, or how frivolous lawsuits can protect consumers? How companies are built, how elections are won, or the role nuclear families and 30-year fixed mortgages play in America?
And even with all this knowledge, can you empathize with both sides of common issues -- the poor renter vs struggling landlord? The tired worker vs underwater business owner? Rich vs poor, immigrant vs legacy, parent vs child -- the list goes on
Each side has both villains and victims. Both landlords and renters can be perpetrators and innocent. Both workers and business owners can be exploited and stolen from.
Yet most people can only identify with one narrative, usually one they've experienced or have a connection to. To acquire, then properly apply this knowledge while honestly detecting your own bias is such an undertaking it's no wonder I only know one or two people capable of it[2].
So it's no surprise humans resort to what’s worked for thousands of years: find our tribe and rep their beliefs, hard.[3]
Why spend weeks or months reading when we can outsource this work to the tribe? It can be our friends, church, or even our favorite news station. Throughout history this method has been so successful we've literally evolved to do it. It's why we laugh when others laugh, run when others start running, want things because others want them -- tribalism is built-in.
But when you acquire opinions in bulk like this, suddenly you don’t have a reasoned view, you have an ideology. Your opinions on sex can predict your opinions on taxation [17]. And it removes the ability to discourse because suddenly learning is replaced with cheering, discovery replaced with winning/losing.
Despite this inherent weakness, overcoming tribalism to improve our reasoning is still doable,
if
we desire. But this brings us to the second, darker reality:
Most people don't
want
to graduate from tribalism.
People don't want to leave the tribe
By far, relationships determine the happiness of ones life, and relationships are not beholden to truth. In fact, they are very commonly built on the opposite.
Whether a boss' reprimands are deserved or not, employees bond over a common enemy. Entire groups form on the basis of beliefs, false or otherwise. We have a word for this: “religion".
Despite organized religion dropping in attendance, religious patterns of behavior are still everywhere, just adapted to a secular world.
Health, exercise, politics, work, self-improvement -- these are all things I've seen friends employ their religious muscle into, across all spectrums and political aisles. And as we get older, I'm seeing more and more of my supposedly-secular friends engage in such behavior[4].
The same religious components are always there:
proclamations of faith
circular reasoning
an evil force (Obama, Elon, Big Pharma, the food industry, corporations, immigrants)

data.title: Evaluating Agent-Based Program Repair at Google
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了基于智能体（agent-based）的程序自动修复技术在企业环境下的应用，特别是针对谷歌内部的软件漏洞修复。通过构建包含178个漏洞的数据集（包括人工报告和机器报告的漏洞），作者实现了Passerine智能体，并利用Gemini 1.5 Pro模型对修复效果进行评估。结果显示，Passerine在机器报告的漏洞中，有73%能生成通过测试的补丁，其中43%的补丁在语义上与真实补丁等价；而在人工报告的漏洞中，这一比例分别为25.6%和17.9%。研究表明，企业环境下的漏洞分布与开源项目存在显著差异，为后续研究提供了基准。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google在BUG数据库中选取部分简单问题测试Gemini 1.5的效果，以及关于自动化补丁生成和测试生成的讨论。

不同观点：
• moqizhengz认为Google选取了相对简单的178个问题来测试Gemini 1.5的性能，并指出这可能只是为了展示其在处理机器检测错误方面的能力。同时，他对建立自动化补丁生成的持续集成管道表示了兴趣，认为这是一个值得探索的方向。
• moqizhengz还提到了论文中提到的另一个实验，即研究代理生成 bug 重现测试的能力，他认为这个实验比当前的测试更为有趣，可能暗示该实验具有更大的研究潜力或应用价值。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了Google的BUG数据库规模（80K），并指出选取的178个问题相对简单，这可能意味着测试结果并不能完全代表Gemini 1.5的整体性能或在更复杂问题上的表现。
• 自动化补丁生成的持续集成管道被认为是未来的一个发展方向，可能有助于提高软件开发和维护的效率。
• 另一个实验，即代理生成bug重现测试的能力，被认为具有更大的研究价值，表明在软件测试和调试自动化方面还有其他值得关注的领域。

争议焦点：目前评论中未直接出现不同观点的对立，但隐含的争议可能是关于Google选取简单问题测试Gemini 1.5的有效性和代表性，这可能不足以全面评估该工具的实际能力。

View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Agent-based program repair offers to automatically resolve complex bugs end-to-end by combining the planning, tool use, and code generation abilities of modern LLMs. Recent work has explored the use of agent-based repair approaches on the popular open-source SWE-Bench, a collection of bugs from highly-rated GitHub Python projects. In addition, various agentic approaches such as SWE-Agent have been proposed to solve bugs in this benchmark. This paper explores the viability of using an agentic approach to address bugs in an enterprise context. To investigate this, we curate an evaluation set of 178 bugs drawn from Google's issue tracking system. This dataset spans both human-reported (78) and machine-reported bugs (100).
To establish a repair performance baseline on this benchmark, we implement Passerine, an agent similar in spirit to SWE-Agent that can work within Google's development environment. We show that with 20 trajectory samples and Gemini 1.5 Pro, Passerine can produce a patch that passes bug tests (i.e., plausible) for 73% of machine-reported and 25.6% of human-reported bugs in our evaluation set. After manual examination, we found that 43% of machine-reported bugs and 17.9% of human-reported bugs have at least one patch that is semantically equivalent to the ground-truth patch.
These results establish a baseline on an industrially relevant benchmark, which as we show, contains bugs drawn from a different distribution -- in terms of language diversity, size, and spread of changes, etc. -- compared to those in the popular SWE-Bench dataset.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于之前讨论的主题（2020年，15条评论）的回顾与分析

不同观点：
• 一方观点认为，2020年的讨论主要围绕技术细节和实际应用，比如有人提到当时讨论了编程语言的性能对比，尤其是Python与C++的性能差异。这部分讨论者关注的是技术实现的可行性和效率问题。

• 另一方观点则指出，讨论中还包含了对技术社区文化的反思，有人认为技术论坛的讨论常常偏离主题，变成个人观点的争论，而非实质性的技术探讨。这部分评论者对讨论的质量和方向提出了质疑。

• 有评论者强调了在2020年的讨论中，有些人提到了技术伦理问题，特别是涉及数据隐私和算法偏见等议题。他们认为技术发展不能只追求效率和性能，还需考虑其社会影响。

• 还有观点认为，那次的讨论反映出社区对新兴技术趋势的关注，比如当时提到了机器学习和人工智能的应用前景，特别是这些技术在商业领域的潜在价值。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于讨论的质量和方向问题。部分参与者认为讨论常常跑题，导致有价值的技术细节被忽视，而另一部分人则认为技术伦理和社会影响等更广泛的议题同样重要，不应被忽视。

• 例子方面，评论中提到了Python与C++性能对比的具体案例，以及关于数据隐私的技术伦理讨论，这些都反映了技术社区在面对实际问题时的不同侧重点。

• 讨论中还有关于技术社区文化的批评与自我反省，部分评论者认为需要更好地引导讨论方向，以确保技术论坛的讨论具有更高的质量和相关性。

data.author: kawera
data.article_summary: NaNoWriMo（美国全国小说写作月）在运营20年后宣布关闭。该非营利组织鼓励参与者在一个月内写出一部5万字的小说，吸引了成千上万的参与者。然而，近年来因财务问题和声誉受损，组织面临困境。2023年，有成员投诉论坛版主不当处理儿童安全问题，尽管涉事版主最终被移除，但引发了更多关于网站儿童安全的投诉。此外，NaNoWriMo对人工智能在写作中使用的立场也引发争议，被指责为“阶级主义和能力歧视”。组织将关闭其网站，但会保留一段时间以便用户获取账户信息，同时表示相信人们会继续在11月写作。

Scandal-hit creative writing website NaNoWriMo to close after 20 years
The US nonprofit, whose online community encouraged members to write a novel in a month, has been rocked by controversy in recent years
Ella Creamer
Wed 2 Apr 2025 09.20 EDT
Last modified on Wed 2 Apr 2025 09.22 EDT
Share
NaNoWriMo, the US-based nonprofit organisation that challenged people to write a novel in a month, has announced it is closing down after 20 years.
NaNoWriMo – an abbreviation of National Novel Writing Month – fostered an online community of participants aiming to write 50,000 words of fiction in November. It began informally in 1999 before becoming a nonprofit in 2006. Each year, tens of thousands signed up to the organisation’s flagship programme.
On Monday, NaNoWriMo announced its closure to community members via email. A 27-minute
YouTube video
posted the same day by the organisation’s interim executive director Kilby Blades explained that it had to close due to ongoing financial problems, which were compounded by reputational damage.
In November 2023, several community members complained to the nonprofit’s board, Blades said. They believed that staff had mishandled accusations made in May 2023 that a NaNoWriMo forum moderator was grooming children on a different website.
The moderator was eventually removed, though this was for unrelated code of conduct violations and occurred “many weeks” after the initial complaints. In the wake of this, community members came forward with other complaints related to child safety on the NaNoWriMo sites.
‘Don’t start a sex scene when your mother-in-law is visiting’: how I wrote a novel in a month
Read more
The organisation was also widely criticised last year over a statement on the use of artificial intelligence in creative writing. After stating that it did not support or explicitly condemn any approach to writing, including the use of AI, it said that the “categorical condemnation of artificial intelligence
has classist and ableist undertones
”.
It went on to say that “not all writers have the financial ability to hire humans to help at certain phases of their writing”, and that “not all brains have same abilities … There is a wealth of reasons why individuals can’t ‘see’ the issues in their writing without help.”
Fantasy author CL Polk
said at the time
that “NaNo is basically asserting that disabled people don’t have what it takes to create art when they trot out the lie that scorning AI is ableist”.
Though the AI controversy received widespread press coverage, Blades’ video primarily focused on the child safety concerns. She said that NaNoWriMo’s position on AI had been covered “frankly so inaccurately”.

The organisation’s closure “will cause no small amount of grief”, said Blades. NaNoWriMo will keep its websites live for “as long as possible” so that “people can take what they want from their accounts”, but did not specify a date when the sites would shut down.
“We hold no belief that people will stop writing 50,000 words in November,” read Monday’s email. “Many alternatives to NaNoWriMo popped up this year, and people did find each other. In so many ways, it’s easier than it was when NaNoWriMo began in 1999 to find your writing tribe online.”
