data.title: Eco Cycles or How I Feel About Technology
data.author: Kvakes
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了技术发展的“生态循环”（Eco Cycle）现象：每一项新技术的出现都伴随着巨大希望，早期使用者受益匪浅，但随着技术普及，问题逐渐显现。作者以传真机、电子邮件和汽车为例，说明这些技术最初带来了便利和自由，但随着广泛使用，却变成了负担和麻烦。传真机被垃圾广告淹没，电子邮件导致信息过载，汽车引发了交通拥堵。研究表明，过度沟通会降低认知能力，而交通拥堵不仅是物理问题，更是心理问题。文章指出，技术成功的同时也会因过度普及而失去最初的优势，形成一种无法摆脱的循环。最终，技术没有解决问题，反而重塑了我们的习惯和期望。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术对个人和社会的影响，以及如何应对技术带来的问题

不同观点：
• [A_Duck] 认为技术产品（如iPad）设计的目标是争取用户的全部注意力，导致成瘾性，尤其是对儿童有负面影响。他建议寻找新的应用和内容创建模式，以保留创新同时减少伤害。
• [FollowingTheDao] 引用了道家思想，认为技术带来的“简便”实际是一种表象，背后隐藏着“困难”。他支持退出技术依赖，通过 stepping out 来赢得生活，而不是紧跟技术潮流。
• [CalRobert] 反对 [FollowingTheDao] 关于交通拥堵的观点，认为通过公共交通、自行车和良好城市设计可以有效解决交通问题，表明技术问题可以通过技术和社会方案解决。
• [Kvakes] 认为技术并非全都能解放人类，很多技术实际上会带来新的束缚，强调技术影响的双面性。
• [c22] 将技术问题归结为“公地悲剧”的旧问题，指出这不仅仅是技术独有的现象，而是普遍存在的资源和管理问题。
• [Miraltar] 引用了《What Technology Wants》中的观点，认为技术像生物系统一样进化，强调技术具有自我发展的趋势。
• [keybored] 批判了硅谷技术专家对于社会问题的“技术决定论”态度，认为他们用技术决定论来解释问题，逃避责任。他强调技术问题是人为造成的，应该通过实际行动解决，而不是通过逃避或归咎于技术决定论。

补充讨论：
• [CalRobert] 提到评论上下文的误解，指出讨论涉及的是Umberto Eco的观点，而不是低水耗洗衣机，表明讨论中存在跨话题的误解。
• [keybored] 进一步指出，技术公司通过吸引用户注意力和时间来谋取利益，这种行为是人为的，而非不可避免的“技术决定论”。他认为社会和技术问题可以通过更好的设计和管理解决，而不是单纯依赖技术暂停或隔离。

争议焦点：
• 技术是否具有不可逆转的“技术决定论”特性，或者问题是否主要由人为因素造成并可以通过人为努力解决。
• 是否可以通过退出或减少技术依赖来解决技术带来的负面影响，还是应该通过更好的技术和社会方案来应对。

43533595.article_content:
Eco Cycles or How I Feel About Technology
28 March 2025
Umberto Eco, the author of
The Name of the Rose
and
Foucault’s Pendulum
(my personal favorite), wasn’t just a brilliant scholar—he was also a bit of a geek. He once wrote an essay comparing Macs to Catholicism and PCs to Protestantism. He thought about technology a lot.
And he loved his fax machine. The ability to send manuscripts to his editor in minutes felt magical. At first.
But the magic didn’t last. Too many people had his number. The machine started spitting out unsolicited ads, junk, spam. Eventually, he just turned it off. What began as a miracle of speed became a firehose of noise.
That story isn’t unique to fax machines. It’s a familiar arc—one we’ve all lived through in different forms.
The Eco Cycle
Every major technology arrives with a promise, and for a while, it delivers. Early adopters ride the wave before anyone else even sees it coming. Imagine driving a car on an empty highway, going wherever you want. Or using the internet in the early 2000s—when it was chaotic, creative, and weird in the best way. If you were there, it felt like a revolution.
But then the crash comes.
Highways clog up. The internet becomes an ad engine. The comment section is a bloodbath, and you're constantly dodging phishing emails.
I call it the Eco Cycle: the lifecycle of a technology that starts as a powerful edge for early adopters and gradually decays into dysfunction as it goes mainstream.
The decay is slow. You don’t wake up one morning and realize the tool has turned on you. It happens drip by drip, feature by feature, until one day you’re not excited anymore—you’re just managing. You’re maintaining.
And by the time you see it, the system has already reshaped your habits, your expectations, your sense of what’s normal.
Technologies That Rode the Curve
Email was a breakthrough. It had the same kind of magic Eco experienced with his fax machine decades earlier. But the magic faded. The problem wasn’t just spam—it was volume. Faxes had friction. Email doesn’t. And when communication becomes nearly free, the floodgates open: low-effort check-ins, reply-all storms, endless CCs.
And email is just one tab. Now we juggle Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, DMs, Discord, LinkedIn messages, calendar invites, and comment threads. Communication didn’t scale insight—it scaled interruption.
Researchers at UC Irvine found that reducing email access lowers stress and improves focus. Other studies show that communication overload reduces cognitive performance—like missing a night of sleep. The effect is real, and measurable.
Email was a symbol of freedom—the ability to talk to anyone, anytime, from anywhere. It promised liberation from gatekeepers, postage, and distance.
Cars made the same promise fifty years ago. If you had one, you could go wherever you wanted, whenever you wanted. Mobility, autonomy, speed.
But the promise didn’t scale. Everyone got a car, and now we sit in traffic. Everyone got email, and now we drown in messages. The thing that once set you free becomes the thing you have to manage—not because it failed, but because it worked too well, for too many people, all at once.
Smartphones were supposed to keep us connected. Now they fragment our attention, mine our behavior, and demand our eyes every waking hour.
Fertilizers boosted crop yields, then wrecked the soil and poisoned the water. Antibiotics saved lives, then gave rise to drug-resistant superbugs. Cheap flights opened the world—and turned the most beautiful places into theme parks.
The pattern is always the same: what begins as a breakthrough becomes, with scale, a burden.
Why We’ll Never Solve Traffic Jams
I can't quite pinpoint the emotion I feel whenever I hear someone talk about solving traffic jams. My therapist thinks it’s because I’m generally not good at naming feelings, so there’s definitely work to do here. Anyhow, it's a strange cocktail: a mix of surprise, annoyance, disapproval of how tax money gets spent, disdain for meaningless conversations. There's quite a bit of ego—"I know better." But I’m working on it.
The thing is, we’ve tried. For decades. Bigger roads, smarter routing, new bypasses. And still, people sit in traffic for hours.
Because traffic isn’t a logistics problem. It’s a psychological one.
We had traffic jams with horses and carts. Then with Model Ts. Now with Teslas. We’ll have them with flying cars, or whatever Elon is cooking up next. Doesn’t matter.
When I lived in San Francisco, I couldn’t wrap my head around the fact that one of my coworkers spent four hours a day commuting. Four. Hours. And he didn’t mind. That’s the point. His tolerance for sitting in traffic was high enough that it was just… normal.
Give that same person a faster car, a smarter road, a flying drone-pod, and they won’t commute for less time. They’ll just live farther out. The metro stretches. The problem scales.
That’s why traffic never goes away. It’s not a bug. It’s baked into us.

data.title: Regulating Imports with a Reciprocal Tariff to Rectify Trade Practices
data.author: vyrotek
data.article_summary:
这篇文章是2025年4月2日由美国总统唐纳德·特朗普发布的行政命令摘要，旨在通过互惠关税来纠正导致美国年度商品贸易逆差过大且持续的贸易行为。特朗普指出，美国与关键贸易伙伴之间的互惠性缺乏、关税率差异和非关税壁垒，以及这些伙伴的经济政策压制国内工资和消费，构成了对美国国家安全和经济的特殊威胁。为此，他宣布国家进入紧急状态，并采取行动应对这些不公平的贸易行为。

文章回顾了自1934年以来美国基于互惠原则的贸易政策历史，指出尽管美国努力降低关税，但与贸易伙伴的关系仍不平衡，导致美国长期存在巨大的商品贸易逆差。这些逆差削弱了美国的制造业基础、关键供应链和国防工业，依赖外国对手。特朗普指示其政府调查逆差原因，并通过互惠关税解决这一问题，以保护美国经济和国家安全。

Presidential Actions
Regulating Imports with a Reciprocal Tariff to Rectify Trade Practices that Contribute to Large and Persistent Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits
Executive Orders
April 2, 2025
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.)(IEEPA), the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.)(NEA), section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended (19 U.S.C. 2483), and section 301 of title 3, United States Code,
I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, find that underlying conditions, including a lack of reciprocity in our bilateral trade relationships, disparate tariff rates and non-tariff barriers, and U.S. trading partners’ economic policies that suppress domestic wages and consumption, as indicated by large and persistent annual U.S. goods trade deficits, constitute an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security and economy of the United States.  That threat has its source in whole or substantial part outside the United States in the domestic economic policies of key trading partners and structural imbalances in the global trading system.  I hereby declare a national emergency with respect to this threat.
On January 20, 2025, I signed the America First Trade Policy Presidential Memorandum directing my Administration to investigate the causes of our country’s large and persistent annual trade deficits in goods, including the economic and national security implications and risks resulting from such deficits, and to undertake a review of, and identify, any unfair trade practices by other countries.  On February 13, 2025, I signed a Presidential Memorandum entitled “Reciprocal Trade and Tariffs,” that directed further review of our trading partners’ non-reciprocal trading practices, and noted the relationship between non-reciprocal practices and the trade deficit.  On April 1, 2025, I received the final results of those investigations, and I am taking action today based on those results.
Large and persistent annual U.S. goods trade deficits have led to the hollowing out of our manufacturing base; inhibited our ability to scale advanced domestic manufacturing capacity; undermined critical supply chains; and rendered our defense-industrial base dependent on foreign adversaries.  Large and persistent annual U.S. goods trade deficits are caused in substantial part by a lack of reciprocity in our bilateral trade relationships.  This situation is evidenced by disparate tariff rates and non-tariff barriers that make it harder for U.S. manufacturers to sell their products in foreign markets.  It is also evidenced by the economic policies of key U.S. trading partners insofar as they suppress domestic wages and consumption, and thereby demand for U.S. exports, while artificially increasing the competitiveness of their goods in global markets.  These conditions have given rise to the national emergency that this order is intended to abate and resolve.
For decades starting in 1934, U.S. trade policy has been organized around the principle of reciprocity.  The Congress directed the President to secure reduced reciprocal tariff rates from key trading partners first through bilateral trade agreements and later under the auspices of the global trading system.  Between 1934 and 1945, the executive branch negotiated and signed 32 bilateral reciprocal trade agreements designed to lower tariff rates on a reciprocal basis.  After 1947 through 1994, participating countries engaged in eight rounds of negotiation, which resulted in the General Agreements on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) and seven subsequent tariff reduction rounds.
However, despite a commitment to the principle of reciprocity, the trading relationship between the United States and its trading partners has become highly unbalanced, particularly in recent years.  The post-war international economic system was based upon three incorrect assumptions:  first, that if the United States led the world in liberalizing tariff and non-tariff barriers the rest of the world would follow; second, that such liberalization would ultimately result in more economic convergence and increased domestic consumption among U.S. trading partners converging towards the share in the United States; and third, that as a result, the United States would not accrue large and persistent goods trade deficits.
This framework set in motion events, agreements, and commitments that did not result in reciprocity or generally increase domestic consumption in foreign economies relative to domestic consumption in the United States.  Those events, in turn, created large and persistent annual U.S. goods trade deficits as a feature of the global trading system.

data.title: Systems Correctness Practices at AWS: Leveraging Formal and Semi-Formal Methods
data.author: yarapavan
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了亚马逊云服务（AWS）如何利用形式化和半形式化方法确保系统正确性。AWS使用TLA+形式规范语言，在开发初期发现并消除潜在缺陷，增强了对系统优化能力的信心。随着规模扩大，AWS整合了形式和半形式方法，如定理证明、模型检查、属性测试、模糊测试和运行时监控。由于TLA+学习曲线陡峭，AWS引入了更易用的P编程语言，用于建模和分析分布式系统。P已在AWS多个核心产品中应用，如S3存储服务的一致性迁移。PObserve工具则进一步帮助验证分布式系统在测试和生产环境中的正确性。这些方法提升了开发效率，确保服务可靠性和性能优化。

Past Issues
Topics
February 4, 2025
Volume 22, issue 6
PDF
Systems Correctness Practices at AWS
Leveraging Formal and Semi-formal Methods
Marc Brooker and Ankush Desai
AWS (Amazon Web Services) strives to deliver reliable services that customers can trust completely. This demands maintaining the highest standards of security, durability, integrity, and availability—with systems correctness serving as the cornerstone for achieving these priorities. An April 2015 paper published in
Communications of the ACM
, titled "How Amazon Web Services Uses Formal Methods," highlighted the approach for ensuring the correctness of critical services that have since become among the most widely used by AWS customers.
21
Central to this approach was TLA+,
14
a formal specification language developed by Leslie Lamport. Our experience at AWS with TLA+ revealed two significant advantages of applying formal methods in practice. First, we could identify and eliminate subtle bugs early in development—bugs that would have eluded traditional approaches like testing. Second, we gained the deep understanding and confidence needed to implement aggressive performance optimizations while maintaining systems correctness.
Moreover, 15 years ago, AWS's software testing practice relied primarily on build-time unit testing, often against mocks, and limited deployment-time integration testing. Since then, we have significantly evolved our correctness practices, integrating both formal and semi-formal approaches into the development process. As AWS has grown, formal methods have become increasingly valuable—not only for ensuring correctness but also for performance improvements, particularly in verifying the correctness of both low- and high-level optimizations. This systematic approach toward systems correctness has become a force multiplier at AWS's scale, enabling faster development cycles through improved developer velocity while delivering more cost-effective services to customers.
This article surveys the portfolio of formal methods used across AWS to deliver complex services with high confidence in its correctness. We consider an umbrella definition of formal methods that encompasses these rigorous techniques—from traditional formal approaches such as theorem proving,
7,10
deductive verification,
18
and model checking
8,14
to more lightweight semi-formal approaches such as property-based testing,
6,19
fuzzing,
9
and runtime monitoring.
11
The P Programming Language
As the use of formal methods was expanded beyond the initial teams at AWS in the early 2010s, we discovered that many engineers struggled to learn and become productive with TLA+. This difficulty seemed to stem from TLA+'s defining feature: It is a high-level, abstract language that more closely resembles mathematics than the imperative programming languages most developers are familiar with. While this mathematical nature is a significant strength of TLA+, and we continue to agree with Lamport's views on the benefits of mathematical thinking,
15
we also sought a language that would allow us to model check (and later prove) key aspects of systems designs while being more approachable to programmers.
We found this balance in the P programming language.
8
P is a state-machine-based language for modeling and analysis of distributed systems. Using P, developers model their system designs as communicating state machines, a mental model familiar to Amazon's developer population, most of whom develop systems based on microservices and SOAs (service-oriented architectures). P has been developed at AWS since 2019 and is maintained as a strategic open-source project.
22
Teams across AWS that build some of its flagship products—from storage (e.g., Amazon S3, EBS), to databases (e.g., Amazon DynamoDB, MemoryDB, Aurora), to compute (e.g., EC2, IoT)—have been using P to reason about the correctness of their system designs.
For example, P was used in migrating S3 (Simple Storage Service) from eventual to strong read-after-write consistency.
1
A key component of S3 is its index subsystem, an object metadata store that enables fast data lookups. To achieve strong consistency, the S3 team had to make several nontrivial changes to the S3 index protocol stack.
25
Because these changes were difficult to get right at S3 scale, and the team wanted to deliver strong consistency with high confidence in correctness, they used P to formally model and validate the protocol design. P helped eliminate several design-level bugs early in the development process and allowed the team to deliver risky optimizations with confidence, as they could be validated using model checking.
In 2023, the P team at AWS built PObserve, which provides a new tool for validating the correctness of distributed systems both during testing and in production. With PObserve, we take structured logs from the execution of distributed systems and validate post-hoc that they match behaviors allowed by the formal P specific

data.title: Show HN: Zig Topological Sort Library for Parallel Processing
data.author: ww520
data.article_summary: TopoSort 是一个高效的 Zig 库，用于对依赖图进行拓扑排序。其主要功能包括：构建依赖图、执行拓扑排序、生成无依赖子集以支持并行处理、检测循环依赖并报告循环、支持不同节点类型。使用步骤包括安装、配置和调用排序功能。安装需从 Releases 页面获取版本并使用 `zig fetch` 命令添加到项目中。使用时需导入库，初始化排序器，添加依赖数据，执行排序并处理结果或检查循环依赖。节点内存由调用者管理，简单类型直接复制，复杂类型如指针不复制内存。TopoSort 还支持配置选项如 `verbose` 和 `max_range` 以优化性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Zig语言、拓扑排序及其在任务调度和并行处理中的应用展开的讨论，包括对现有工具的实现、优化和性能的分析。

不同观点：
• Cieric认为Zig在很多情况下优于C/C++，但目前还缺少一些关键功能（如comptime的某些特性），这限制了其在大型项目中的应用。他正在考虑是等待这些功能的实现还是自行 fork 并添加所需功能。此外，他对如何处理循环依赖（cycle detection）以及节点重复计算的问题表示关注。
• jitl讨论了拓扑排序在任务调度中的实际应用，指出当前按集合顺序调度的方式可能导致任务饥饿问题。他认为应该更加关注实际调度的优化，比如在任务完成时动态检查依赖并启动相关任务，而不是仅仅依赖预先排序的集合。
• emmanueloga_解释了拓扑排序的基本原理，包括只有无环有向图（DAGs）才能进行拓扑排序，以及如何通过深度优先搜索（DFS）实现拓扑排序，并提供了JavaScript的实现示例。他还提到了如何检测图中的循环依赖。
• chubot提到Python标准库中已有一个用于拓扑排序的模块（graphlib），并表示对该模块的实际应用效果感兴趣。
• tediousgraffit1对项目表示赞赏，尤其提到了实现命令行接口（CLI）而不仅仅是测试用例的价值，认为这是一个探索新技术的理想规模项目。
• duped讨论了并行任务调度的复杂性，指出图切割方法可能导致资源利用率低，并提出了基于Kahn算法的并发任务调度方法。他还提到了更多优化和启发式方法的可能性，并对如何在库中实现无依赖子集的并行处理表示关注。
• hbbio对Zig表示喜爱，并提到他们曾在TypeScript中实现了一个类似的图处理库，作为其项目的一部分。

TopoSort - Topological Sort on Dependency Graph
TopoSort is a highly efficient Zig library for performing topological sort on dependency graph.  This small library is packed with the following features:
Building dependency graph from dependency data.
Performing topological sort on the dependency graph.
Generating dependence-free subsets for parallel processing.
Cycle detection and cycle reporting.
Support different node types.

43549618.article_summary: TopoSort 是一个高效的 Zig 库，用于对依赖图进行拓扑排序。其主要功能包括：构建依赖图、执行拓扑排序、生成无依赖子集以支持并行处理、检测循环依赖并报告循环、支持不同节点类型。使用步骤包括安装、配置和调用排序功能。安装需从 Releases 页面获取版本并使用 `zig fetch` 命令添加到项目中。使用时需导入库，初始化排序器，添加依赖数据，执行排序并处理结果或检查循环依赖。节点内存由调用者管理，简单类型直接复制，复杂类型如指针不复制内存。TopoSort 还支持配置选项如 `verbose` 和 `max_range` 以优化性能。

data.title: DIY Synths Database
data.author: guardienaveugle
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个精选集，包含75种适合DIY的硬件合成器及相关独立音乐设备。所有项目均为开源，意味着设计和代码公开，允许用户自行制作、修改和学习。这些合成器和设备适合音乐爱好者和电子工程师，提供了从基础到复杂的多种选择，旨在促进音乐创作的开放性和可访问性。通过开源社区的共享，用户可以互相学习、改进设计，推动创新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源和DIY合成器的项目和资源

不同观点：
• Parae认为Korg NTS-1虽然不是完全开源，但仍然具有可修改性，因为Korg提供了C和C++ SDK，且这种合成器是自组装套件。他还提到x0xb0x的有趣开源条款。
• kzalesak询问如何将自己的数字合成器项目（Digisynth）添加到集合中，或者需要哪些更改才能符合条件。
• chrissoundz提供了另一个类似的项目（bom-squad.com），并提到整个网站的代码都在GitHub上，且自己曾参与该项目。
• guardienaveugle分享了自己构建ardutouch的经历，并推荐其作为初学者的硬件项目。
• Fraterkes推荐了一个非常易于DIY的合成器项目（m8 headless build），并详细描述了构建过程和成本。
• lomase感谢Mutable Instruments提供了DSP代码。
• kbouck询问是否有人尝试过SC1000，并表示自己想将其改造成MIDI控制器而不是独立音乐设备。
• myky22分享了自己使用Yamaha Seqtrak和OP-XY的经历，并表示对NTS-1有深入研究。
• lavela建议如果数据库扩展，应该能够排除某些标签，例如排除模块化相关的内容。
• m_kos寻找非常实惠的DIY MIDI控制表面，要求具有一些旋钮、垫子、键（两个八度）和蓝牙功能。
• chr15m简单表达了对目录的赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 项目和资源的分享与推荐是讨论的核心，许多评论者提供了自己构建或使用的相关项目链接和经验。
• 开源和可修改性的定义在讨论中有所涉及，Parae提到Korg NTS-1虽然不是完全开源，但仍具有DIY和可修改的特性。
• 争议焦点不明显，但不同用户的需求和偏好（例如模块化内容的排除与否）反映了不同用户在DIY合成器项目中的多样性。
• 一些用户（如kzalesak和kbouck）对如何将自己的项目或修改纳入讨论集合表现出兴趣。

data.title: US Administration announces 34% tariffs on China, 20% on EU
data.author: belter
data.article_summary: 唐纳德·特朗普对所有进口到美国的商品征收10%的关税，部分被视为“最大违规者”的国家则面临更高关税。此举引发全球广泛批评，欧盟称其为对世界经济的重大打击，中国誓言报复，澳大利亚和意大利等国也表示不满。具体关税包括：欧盟20%，中国54%，日本24%，而加拿大和墨西哥暂不受影响。此外，所有外国产汽车将被加征25%关税。全球市场对此反应负面，亚洲市场下跌后略有回升。英国担忧此举可能影响就业，尤其是汽车和制药行业。特朗普称关税反映了各国对美国的贸易壁垒，但实际更多基于贸易逆差。全球担忧贸易战可能加剧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国白宫发布的关税政策及其潜在经济影响

不同观点：
• **toasterlovin**：引用了白宫的"半官方"数据，指出关税将从4月5日开始实施，但对"最严重违规者"的关税率尚未明确。他认为，在海关和边境保护局发布关税率之前，这些数据都不算正式。
• **ggm**：认为政府完全明白关税政策的经济后果，并有意通过这些政策来重置经济，例如通过美元重估来减少外债。尽管这种策略有风险，但政府可能认为可以控制短期冲击，以实现长期经济重置。
• **TrackerFF**：强调了取消最低免税额的影响，特别是对中国进口商品加征30%的关税，可能导致消费者在接收订单时面临额外账单，进而引发市场混乱。
• **mcoliver**：提供了有关关税数据的详细信息，指出这些关税实际上是基于贸易不平衡的百分比，而非传统意义上的关税。
• **phillipseamore**：认为10%的最低关税为本地制造商提供了涨价的借口，并以自己所在国家的经验为例，说明即使关税取消后，价格也可能不会显著下降。
• **iteratethis**：指出美国缺乏制造业劳动力，即使关税政策成功吸引制造业回流，也可能面临劳动力短缺的问题。
• **pjmlp**：预期其他国家将采取报复性关税，并担心政府可能会对软件出口施加限制。
• **seydor**：批评去全球化政策，认为这将导致愚蠢的贸易转移，例如其他国家通过英国转售商品以规避关税。
• **hnburnsy**：列举了不受关税政策影响的商品类别，包括钢铁、铝制品、汽车零部件等。
• **jenadine**：询问关税政策是否会影响软件服务，并探讨了通过第三国进行贸易仲裁的可能性。
• **olejorgenb**：质疑将增值税（VAT）视为关税的逻辑，并比较了美国各州的消费税与VAT的相似性。
• **gigatexal**：认为过去50年制造业外流对美国工人造成了伤害，但通过对盟友加征关税可能导致经济衰退，不如通过美元贬值和生产补贴来支持国内制造业。
• **tnt128**：不同意关税总是由消费者承担的观点，认为如果公司有其他采购选择，可能会迫使中国供应商降价。
• **fabian2k**：询问新关税是否叠加在现有关税之上，并担心韩国、台湾等地的电子产品以及越南、柬埔寨、孟加拉国等国的廉价商品将受到影响。
• **r00fus**：认为关税是对消费品的征税，将对经济成长产生负面影响。

补充讨论：
• **关税的实施细节和影响**：不同用户对关税的具体实施方式和可能带来的市场混乱表示关注，尤其是对最低免税额取消后的影响。
• **关税的目的和后果**：部分用户认为关税政策是为了经济重置，有意通过短期冲击实现长期经济目标，但也有用户担心这会适得其反，导致经济衰退和消费者负担增加。
• **劳动力问题**：有用户指出，即使制造业回流，美国也面临劳动力短缺的问题，这对制造业复苏构成挑战。
• **国际反应**：预期其他国家将采取报复性关税措施，并担心政策扩展到软件出口限制。

争议焦点：

Donald Trump imposes
universal 10% tariff
on all imports into the US, with even higher rates for what he calls the
"worst offenders"
, in a watershed moment for global trade
The EU describes it as a
"major blow to the world economy"

Three things to know about Trump's tariffs announcement
Live Reporting

Image source,

The US is bringing in sweeping new tariffs on goods from around the world. Here are the key points:
A 10% baseline rate
A minimum 10% tariff will apply to most countries, including the UK, Australia, Argentina and Saudi Arabia. It's set to start on 5 April.
Country-specific rates
Roughly 60 countries the US sees as the "worst offenders" will face specific "reciprocal" tariffs. The US says these were calculated using a formula based on what it sees as unfair trade practices. These come into effect on 9 April. Examples include:
European Union: 20%
China: 54%
Japan: 24%
No new tariffs for Canada and Mexico
The White House says it will deal with both countries through an already announced framework, which includes 25% tariffs with some exceptions.
Cars to get 25% tariffs
A 25% tariff on all foreign-made cars was also put in place and came into effect at midnight on 3 April.
Other specified products - such as steel and aluminium - will retain tariff rates already set.

43561253.article_summary: 唐纳德·特朗普对所有进口到美国的商品征收10%的关税，部分被视为“最大违规者”的国家则面临更高关税。此举引发全球广泛批评，欧盟称其为对世界经济的重大打击，中国誓言报复，澳大利亚和意大利等国也表示不满。具体关税包括：欧盟20%，中国54%，日本24%，而加拿大和墨西哥暂不受影响。此外，所有外国产汽车将被加征25%关税。全球市场对此反应负面，亚洲市场下跌后略有回升。英国担忧此举可能影响就业，尤其是汽车和制药行业。特朗普称关税反映了各国对美国的贸易壁垒，但实际更多基于贸易逆差。全球担忧贸易战可能加剧。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：全民基本收入（UBI）的可行性、资金来源、宏观经济影响以及可能的替代方案。

不同观点：
• [notepad0x90] 认为应排除情绪化讨论，专注于UBI是否是纳税资金的最佳使用方式。他强调需要数据和研究来证明UBI对各系统（如警察部门、社会福利服务等）的实际影响，并提出是否可以有一种替代方案，让有劳动能力的人参与劳动池。
• [jimnotgym] 认为UBI作为货币政策工具比量化宽松（QE）更有效，因为UBI直接进入低收入家庭，迅速刺激经济。
• [bsenftner] 持强烈反对意见，认为UBI会固化低伦理标准，并导致经济停滞，消除经济上升的可能性，是一种宏观经济的毒药。
• [mertbio] 提出UBI不是解决住房问题的有效方案，建议实施"全民基本土地"（Universal Basic Land）政策。
• [veltas] 担心UBI会导致高需求商品价格上涨，最终对穷人不利，强调需要关注如何阻止穷人变得更穷。
• [KolmogorovComp] 质疑如果UBI的最高可持续水平很低（如10美元），是否还有实际意义，并引用数据支持其观点。
• [dwighttk] 质疑UBI的资金来源，以阿拉斯加通过出售石油实现UBI为例，提出广泛实施UBI的资金来源问题。
• [throw0101b] 引用Luke Martinelli的论文，提出UBI面临的可负担性、充足性和保留福利的全面优势三难选择（trilemma），认为部分BI方案可能需要放弃一些关键优势。
• [6510] 认为单靠利率调控经济不理想，建议从小额UBI（如10美元）开始，以获取实施数据和解决实际问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于UBI是否能够有效帮助经济弱势群体，以及是否会导致经济负面影响。支持者强调其直接经济刺激作用，反对者担心其长期经济后果和实施成本。
• 替代方案如"全民基本土地"和劳动池方案也被提出，作为UBI的可能替代或补充。
• 资金来源和UBI的具体实施细节也是讨论的核心，包括如何避免对经济的不利影响和高需求商品价格上涨。

data.title: Efficient light control: Meta-optics replace conventional lenses
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了卡尔斯鲁厄理工学院（KIT）开发的元光学（meta-optics）技术，该技术使用超构表面（metasurfaces）替代传统曲面透镜，实现更高效的光控制。元表面由微小的 meta-原子组成，能够精准调控光的相位、振幅和偏振，从而在更小的体积内实现多项光学功能。该技术可用于制造光学衍射元光栅，其效率是传统光栅的四倍，特别适用于光谱学、电信和激光系统等领域。此外，元光学在相机、传感器、增强现实显示、材料分选、医疗成像和自动驾驶等应用中也展现出广阔前景。该技术利用半导体行业的先进光刻和蚀刻技术，具备可扩展生产潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：meta-optics技术是否具有实际应用价值和前景

不同观点：
• CyberDildonics认为，所谓的“meta光学”、“meta表面”和“meta光栅”并没有实际取代现有的技术和产品。这暗示了对meta-optics技术实际应用效果的怀疑，认为其在市场或技术领域中并没有产生显著影响。

• ipsum2指出，尽管meta-lenses（元透镜）技术已经存在超过10年，但目前仍未见到任何消费级商业产品使用这种技术。这进一步质疑meta-optics技术的商业可行性和普及程度，认为其缺乏实际应用或市场接受度。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于meta-optics技术的实用性和市场前景。一方认为该技术没有实现取代传统技术的承诺，另一方则通过缺乏消费级产品的事实来进一步质疑其商业价值。
• 时间因素被提及（技术存在超过10年），这增加了对技术发展缓慢或受阻的质疑。
• 缺乏具体应用实例成为讨论中的一个关键点，双方都基于这一事实提出了对meta-optics技术前景的怀疑。

Efficient light control: Meta-optics replace conventional lenses
by Martin Heidelberger,
Karlsruhe Institute of Technology
Advanced light control: A laser beam hits a meta-grating that directs the light waves even at steep incidence angles, thus enabling new optical applications. Credit: Maryna Leonidivna Meretska
Conventional curved lenses, which direct light by refraction in glass or plastic, are often bulky and heavy, offering only limited control of light waves. Metasurfaces, in contrast, are flat and consist of an array of tiny structures known as meta-atoms. Meta-atoms influence light at a subwavelength scale and thus allow for highly precise control of the phase, amplitude, and polarization of light.
"Using metasurfaces, we can influence the temporal shift, intensity, and direction of oscillation of light waves in a targeted way," says Dr. Maryna Leonidivna Meretska, Group Leader at KIT's Institute of Nanotechnology.
"Thanks to its multiplex control capabilities, i.e., the simultaneous and targeted influencing of various parameters, a single metasurface can replace multiple
optical components
. Thus, the size of the optical system can be reduced without affecting its performance."
Production will also be simpler, "Metasurfaces can be manufactured using advanced lithography and etching technologies from the
semiconductor industry
, making scalable production possible," says Meretska.
Meta-grating with a fourfold increase in efficiency
At
Hannover Messe
, which begins Monday, March 31, Meretska and her team will present an optical diffraction meta-grating that was made using special KIT manufacturing equipment. Diffraction gratings are essential optical components that can be used in various industrial applications, such as spectroscopy, telecommunications, and laser systems.
Usually, the efficiency of diffraction gratings decreases sharply as the angle of incidence of the light increases. The meta-grating developed at KIT is four times more efficient than conventional systems.
"Our meta-grating offers unprecedented control of light under challenging conditions. This represents a significant advance for future applications requiring precise light control," says Meretska. As the functionality has been proven with the prototype, the research group is currently developing targeted optical solutions for various industrial applications.
A wide range of applications
The flat structure of meta-optical components makes them particularly suitable for cameras, sensors, and augmented-reality displays, as they offer improved functionality while reducing the size of optical systems.
Other potential applications include materials sorting and
quality control
, medical imaging, microscopy, and solar cells. In addition, robotics and autonomous driving, both relying on
object recognition
, might benefit considerably from the technological advances of meta-optics.

Karlsruhe Institute of Technology

• 缺乏具体应用实例成为讨论中的一个关键点，双方都基于这一事实提出了对meta-optics技术前景的怀疑。

data.title: Reintroducing Capsul
data.author: j3s
data.article_summary: Capsul起源自cyberia.club，最初名为CVM（Cyberia Virtual Machines），通过手工创建虚拟机并收费。服务器“Baikal”因其深层含义而得名，并在初期运行良好。随着Forest开发了自助网页界面，CVM更名为Capsul。由于硬件问题，团队曾赴亚特兰大修复服务器。在遭遇Stripe支付中断后，Capsul从Cyberia独立出来，由新成立的Break Software LLC运营。2025年，新服务器Rathouse上线，团队计划通过改进性能和功能，使Capsul成为更优质、易用的小型云服务，而非简单的租赁平台。未来发展仍在不断推进中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：虚拟机 provisioning 前端的开源情况及相关工具的用户体验

不同观点：
• Pomatic 关心虚拟机 provisioning 前端是否开源或部分开源，其主要目的是寻找一个可以灵活调整的后台框架，而不是像 Proxmox 那样虽然有友好的用户界面但难以在后台进行自定义调整。Pomatic 强调他并非想复制业务，而是寻找一个更具操作性的解决方案。

• Simorgh 则偏离了开源话题，转而对一个网页（链接：https://capsul.org/）的用户体验（UX）表示赞赏。他认为该页面的设计感强，给人一种置身于“真实网站”的感觉，尤其对页面的色调、易理解性以及整体的视觉冲击力表示肯定。

补充讨论：
• Pomatic 的评论主要集中在技术实现和开源问题上，关注的是软件的功能性和可操作性。

43534381.article_content:
reintroducing capsul
29 Mar, 2025
capsul
has a rich history. born through
cyberia.club
, our first server was literally cobbled together on the rooftop of my apartment complex. about 10 of us were there, perhaps a little drunk, and we covered the first 1u server in stickers. it's still around the clubhouse at
layer zero
- we named the server "baikal", after the deepest lake in the world, and a joke on "cyberia" sounding like "siberia". here is a picture of baikal from back then:
when capsul started, it wasn't even called capsul - it was called "cvm", which stood for "cyberia virtual machines".
i created virtual machines for people by hand with a small set of shell scripts, and those people paid me in cash. cvm was cool like that - covert, human, and communal. i'd take 60 bux, write it down in a spreadsheet, and spin up a VM.
some vms still have a
cvm-
prefix internally.
eventually,
forest
came along and blessed cvm with a self-service web interface. at this point, we renamed cvm to capsul. it took forest about a week to pump out capsul v1, which looked like this:
baikal + capsul ran many virtual machines for many people for nearly five years, with only a few minor mishaps along the way.
well, except...
atlanta
one time, the disks in baikal were basically about to explode themselves
, and we were too embarassed ask the
CyberWurx
datacenter staff to try to help us fix it remotely after we had mailed them two different PCI-E SSD risers that didn't fit in the server chassis. So we had to fly to Atlanta (where baikal was in a rack at CyberWurx) to fix them. forest and i made a little trip of it:
in the end, we prevailed. we prevented a critical storage mishap, and baikal lived on for another several years.
EPIC emergency server migration 🤯
baikal (our old server) could no longer handle the load, was constantly crashing
rathouse (our NEW server) was already racked up and ready to go
we wanted to wait until we could get backups working on the new system before we migrated... but real life had other plans for us
capsul was fully down for about a day and a half
stripe doomsday
stripe cut off our credit card payments because the cyberia computer club's minnesota nonprofit status had lapsed after everyone who was doing the work of maintaining it faded away.
we had been the ones maintaining capsul for many years at that point, and in 2023, cyberia congress
officially released
capsul to be owned by us instead of being owned by the club.
so in order to get stripe payments working again, we "failed forward" and created a new legal entity that will be responsible for operating capsul:
break software llc
future
okay, so it's 2025. we recently installed a new server (rathouse), and have renewed energy for this project. forest and i are getting more serious about trying to make capsul a real thing.
we've been talking with great folks around various smallweb communities -- the kind of folks capsul was originally created for, and who we still want to offer a great service to. it's always been like this; we use capsul ourselves, and our own wants and needs as admins of an
independent community-hosting project
have guided capsul's development:
we needed better storage performance to make our chat server happy, so we adjusted the storage settings to speed up our disk reads and writes as much as possible.
we still wanted to be able to back up and restore our VMs, so we integrated
virtnbdbackup
directly into capsul.
we want to make capsul the best lil cloud there is. not just another 5$/month rent seeking project;  a genuinely better option which is more accessible, more fun, and still has the power and reliability to be much more than a toy.
we gave capsul a CSS makeover, a light theme, fixed some longstanding bugs, and updated all of our OS images, and we have a lot of ideas, but they're still baking.
if you wanna say hi, you can always send us email at
support@capsul.org
-- otherwise, we're always hanging out in
matrix
. :)
i'll try to post here at least monthly.
see you soon <3 <3 <3
love,
j3s
,
forest
10

data.title: Aptera's First Solar Road Trip. 300 Miles, One Charge
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: Aptera成功完成了其首次太阳能支持的公路旅行，单次充电行驶超过300英里，展示了太阳能电动车不仅是未来概念，更是当前可行的解决方案。这趟旅程从亚利桑那州的弗拉格斯塔夫出发，经过历史悠久的66号公路，途经金曼和哈瓦苏湖，最终返回加州。尽管有些时候是多云天气，车辆仍能产生超过545瓦的太阳能输入。车辆在各种路况下表现优异，包括山路、高速公路和乡村道路。此次旅行不仅验证了Aptera系统在现实条件下的可靠性，还展示了重新思考交通工具的潜力。为了庆祝这次成功，Aptera还举办了一项抽奖活动，奖品包括价值800美元的太阳能套装。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Aptera太阳能汽车的愿景、可行性及其市场前景

不同观点：
• 支持并赞赏Aptera的愿景：
   - [arrakark] 认为人们对Aptera外观和三轮设计的批评只是因为汽车被当作身份象征，生产问题才是真正值得担心的。
   - [underseacables] 对Aptera充满热情，但担心其融资问题，并指出政府贷款项目的失败对公司造成了影响。

• 对市场接受度的怀疑：
   - [mlsu] 认为Aptera的设计虽美，但不符合大众市场需求，大多数消费者更注重汽车的实用性和身份象征。

• 对技术可行性的质疑：
   - [quailfarmer] 指出太阳能车概念并不新颖，质疑Aptera的创新性。
   - [pinkmuffinere] 通过计算质疑太阳能板在实际情况下提供的续航能力，认为其实用性有限，但希望被证明错误。

• 对商业成功的担忧：
   - [jore] 提到德国公司Sono Sion的失败案例，虽然对Aptera抱有希望，但对其商业前景持谨慎态度。

• 对设计细节的批评：
   - [dontlaugh] 质疑车辆尺寸，认为作为高效车，车身过大。

• 对太阳能应用的现实评估：
   - [ZeroGravitas] 认为太阳能板在特定领域有意义，但对Aptera的目标市场不清楚。
   - [trhway] 通过数据分析，认为太阳能板在现实中提供的续航有限，但并非完全没有意义。
   - [dscottboggs] 强烈批评太阳能板在实际驾驶中的效果，认为太阳能车不切实际，只适合辅助系统。

补充讨论：
• Aptera的生产和融资问题是多个评论者关注的焦点，担心其能否成功进入市场。
• 对太阳能技术在汽车上的应用存在争议，部分人认为技术有潜力但成本高，部分人则认为完全不切实际。

43533556.article_content:
300+ Miles, One Charge, Supported by the Sun’s Rays
Aptera just completed its first-ever solar-supported road trip—driving over 300 miles on a single charge and proving that a solar EV isn’t just a concept for the future, but a real-world solution ready for the present.
Our Co-CEO Steve Fambro, along with a small crew, took Aptera’s production-intent vehicle on a road trip through the American Southwest. They started early in the snowy mountain town of Flagstaff, Arizona, where the vehicle was already pulling in 300 watts of solar energy before the day even began.
The route followed a stretch of historic Route 66—quiet roads, breathtaking scenery, and a test bed for a vehicle built to thrive independently. “It’s kind of the path not really taken,” Steve shared. “And that’s one of the reasons we wanted to do it this way.”
From Flagstaff to Hackberry, through Kingman and down to sunny Lake Havasu, Aptera performed with quiet confidence. Even on an overcast day, the team saw over 545 watts of solar input. That means more time exploring and less time searching for chargers.
During its 300+ mile journey, the vehicle handled every condition thrown at it: mountain passes, 18-wheelers, potholes, desert winds, highways, and winding country roads.
“The panoramic windshield gives you this incredible view of the landscape,” Steve said, describing the drive. “It’s like a big picture window into the future.”
The final stretch took the team back into California, where they reflected on the journey, the data, and the excited reactions from drivers who caught a glimpse of the vehicle on the road. “Almost everyone we passed had their phones out filming us,” Steve laughed. “It’s clear that Aptera’s design stops traffic—without needing to stop for a charge.”
This trip marks a huge milestone for Aptera, not only in validating our systems in real-world conditions but in showing what’s possible when you rethink transportation from the ground up. With every mile driven by our production-intent vehicles, we’re one step closer to a future where every journey is powered by the sun.

data.title: Dijkstra On the foolishness of "natural language programming"
data.author: nimbleplum40
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了“自然语言编程”的不可行性。作者认为，从早期计算开始，人们抱怨编程需要精确和严谨，希望机器能自动纠正错误指令。虽然高级编程语言和错误提示改善了部分问题，但机器仍会忠实执行无意义指令。有人提议用自然语言编程以简化操作，但这会增加机器的复杂性。作者质疑这种观点，指出历史上数学的发展得益于形式符号的使用，而非自然语言。希腊和穆斯林数学的停滞正是因为缺乏符号化，而西方数学的进步则归功于形式化符号。因此，形式符号实际上是一种有效工具，帮助排除错误和无意义的内容。自然语言的“自然性”反而使其易于产生无意义陈述。文章最后推测，若从一开始就用自然语言与计算机交互，计算机科学可能难以发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在代码和自然语言之间转换的有效性及自然语言在编程中的适用性

不同观点：
• [01100011] 认为将中等复杂度的代码转换回自然语言描述，可能会丢失细节，无法完整再现程序。自然语言难以处理高复杂度和精确度要求，法律语言的复杂性即是例子。
• [l0new0lf-G] 支持上述观点，指出自然语言有内在的局限性，人类的思维有时过于抽象或具体，导致遗漏重要细节。编程语言在表达严格符号方面更有效。
• [wiz21c] 提出教育趋势导致人们语言掌握能力下降，可能影响自然语言在编程中的应用效果。
• [jedimastert] 指出编程中自然语言的使用并不直观，且某些错误提示比错误结果更让人反感，暗示对自然语言编程工具的适应困难。
• [misja111] 认为在企业中，新功能的构思通常来自非技术人员，因此从自然语言到形式语言的翻译不可避免，AI可以帮助完成这一过程。
• [hamstergene] 通过多个历史案例（如用流程图代替代码、弱类型语言等）说明某些看似简化的自然语言编程思路在实践中往往导致复杂性和生产力问题。
• [odyssey7] 以戏谑的方式提出管理者存在的必要性问题，暗示编程比自然语言交流更直接有效。
• [haolez] 引用Hal Abelson的观点，强调计算机科学作为一种思维方式的变革，计算提供了处理“如何做”的框架，而不仅仅是“是什么”。
• [octacat] 认为自然语言在描述复杂系统的技术需求和预期功能方面有优势，但编程语言在自动化和计算机环境中更为实用。
• [Rodmine] 认为用自然语言描述任务是可行的，但任务的可行性是另一问题，并通过实例说明目前技术下自然语言生成代码的成功案例。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于自然语言在编程中是否能有效替代形式语言，支持者认为自然语言更易理解和沟通，反对者则指出其在复杂性和精确度上的局限。
• 讨论中还涉及历史上的类似尝试及其失败教训，警示不应重复无效的思路。
• 对AI工具在编程中的实际应用效果存在不同看法，有人认为其可帮助完成从自然语言到代码的转换，有人则质疑其实际可行性和适应性。

EWD 667
On the foolishness of "natural language programming"
.
Since the early days of automatic computing we have had people that have felt it as a shortcoming that programming required the care and accuracy that is characteristic for the use of any formal symbolism. They blamed the mechanical slave for its strict obedience with which it carried out its given instructions, even if a moment's thought would have revealed that those instructions contained an obvious mistake. "But a moment is a long time, and thought is a painful process." (A.E.Houseman). They eagerly hoped and waited for more sensible machinery that would refuse to embark on such nonsensical activities as a trivial clerical error evoked at the time.
Machine code, with its absence of almost any form of redundancy, was soon identified as a needlessly risky interface between man and machine. Partly in response to this recognition so-called "high-level programming languages" were developed, and, as time went by, we learned to a certain extent how to enhance the protection against silly mistakes. It was a significant improvement that now many a silly mistake did result in an error message instead of in an erroneous answer. (And even this improvement wasn't universally appreciated: some people found error messages they couldn't ignore more annoying than wrong results, and, when judging the relative merits of programming languages, some still seem to equate "the ease of programming" with the ease of making undetected mistakes.) The (abstract) machine corresponding to a programming language remained, however, a faithful slave, i.e. the nonsensible automaton perfectly capable of carrying out nonsensical instructions. Programming remained the use of a formal symbolism and, as such, continued to require the care and accuracy required before.
In order to make machines significantly easier to use, it has been proposed (to try) to design machines that we could instruct in our native tongues. this would, admittedly, make the machines much more complicated, but, it was argued, by letting the machine carry a larger share of the burden, life would become easier for us. It sounds sensible provided you blame the obligation to use a formal symbolism as the source of your difficulties. But is the argument valid? I doubt.
We know in the meantime that the choice of an interface is not just a division of (a fixed amount of) labour, because the work involved in co-operating and communicating across the interface has to be added. We know in the meantime —from sobering experience, I may add— that a change of interface can easily increase at both sides of the fence the amount of work to be done (even drastically so). Hence the increased preference for what are now called "narrow interfaces". Therefore, although changing to communication between machine and man conducted in the latter's native tongue would greatly increase the machine's burden, we have to challenge the assumption that this would simplify man's life.
A short look at the history of mathematics shows how justified this challenge is. Greek mathematics got stuck because it remained a verbal, pictorial activity, Moslem "algebra", after a timid attempt at symbolism, died when it returned to the rhetoric style, and the modern civilized world could only emerge —for better or for worse— when Western Europe could free itself from the fetters of medieval scholasticism —a vain attempt at verbal precision!— thanks to the carefully, or at least consciously designed formal symbolisms that we owe to people like Vieta, Descartes, Leibniz, and (later) Boole.
The virtue of formal texts is that their manipulations, in order to be legitimate, need to satisfy only a few simple rules; they are, when you come to think of it, an amazingly effective tool for ruling out all sorts of nonsense that, when we use our native tongues, are almost impossible to avoid.
Instead of regarding the obligation to use formal symbols as a burden, we should regard the convenience of using them as a privilege: thanks to them, school children can learn to do what in earlier days only genius could achieve. (This was evidently not understood by the author that wrote —in 1977— in the preface of a technical report that "even the standard symbols used for logical connectives have been avoided for the sake of clarity". The occurrence of that sentence suggests that the author's misunderstanding is not confined to him alone.) When all is said and told, the "naturalness" with which we use our native tongues boils down to the ease with which we can use them for making statements the nonsense of which is not obvious.
It may be illuminating to try to imagine what would have happened if, right from the start our native tongue would have been the only vehicle for the input into and the output from our information processing equipment. My considered guess is that history would, in a sense, have repeated itself, and that computer science would consist mainly of the in
43564386.article_summary: 文章讨论了“自然语言编程”的不可行性。作者认为，从早期计算开始，人们抱怨编程需要精确和严谨，希望机器能自动纠正错误指令。虽然高级编程语言和错误提示改善了部分问题，但机器仍会忠实执行无意义指令。有人提议用自然语言编程以简化操作，但这会增加机器的复杂性。作者质疑这种观点，指出历史上数学的发展得益于形式符号的使用，而非自然语言。希腊和穆斯林数学的停滞正是因为缺乏符号化，而西方数学的进步则归功于形式化符号。因此，形式符号实际上是一种有效工具，帮助排除错误和无意义的内容。自然语言的“自然性”反而使其易于产生无意义陈述。文章最后推测，若从一开始就用自然语言与计算机交互，计算机科学可能难以发展。
43564386.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在代码和自然语言之间转换的有效性及自然语言在编程中的适用性

不同观点：
• [01100011] 认为将中等复杂度的代码转换回自然语言描述，可能会丢失细节，无法完整再现程序。自然语言难以处理高复杂度和精确度要求，法律语言的复杂性即是例子。
• [l0new0lf-G] 支持上述观点，指出自然语言有内在的局限性，人类的思维有时过于抽象或具体，导致遗漏重要细节。编程语言在表达严格符号方面更有效。
• [wiz21c] 提出教育趋势导致人们语言掌握能力下降，可能影响自然语言在编程中的应用效果。
• [jedimastert] 指出编程中自然语言的使用并不直观，且某些错误提示比错误结果更让人反感，暗示对自然语言编程工具的适应困难。
• [misja111] 认为在企业中，新功能的构思通常来自非技术人员，因此从自然语言到形式语言的翻译不可避免，AI可以帮助完成这一过程。
• [hamstergene] 通过多个历史案例（如用流程图代替代码、弱类型语言等）说明某些看似简化的自然语言编程思路在实践中往往导致复杂性和生产力问题。
• [odyssey7] 以戏谑的方式提出管理者存在的必要性问题，暗示编程比自然语言交流更直接有效。
• [haolez] 引用Hal Abelson的观点，强调计算机科学作为一种思维方式的变革，计算提供了处理“如何做”的框架，而不仅仅是“是什么”。
• [octacat] 认为自然语言在描述复杂系统的技术需求和预期功能方面有优势，但编程语言在自动化和计算机环境中更为实用。
• [Rodmine] 认为用自然语言描述任务是可行的，但任务的可行性是另一问题，并通过实例说明目前技术下自然语言生成代码的成功案例。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于自然语言在编程中是否能有效替代形式语言，支持者认为自然语言更易理解和沟通，反对者则指出其在复杂性和精确度上的局限。
• 讨论中还涉及历史上的类似尝试及其失败教训，警示不应重复无效的思路。
• 对AI工具在编程中的实际应用效果存在不同看法，有人认为其可帮助完成从自然语言到代码的转换，有人则质疑其实际可行性和适应性。

data.title: XWine1 – Xbox One Translation Layer for Windows PCs
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: XDLCompiler是一个由XWine1组织的开源项目，是用C#编写的XDL语言编译器。该项目拥有84个提交，最近一次更新是在2025年3月22日，采用MIT许可证。目前，该组织没有公开成员。XDLCompiler的主要技术栈为C#，但具体使用主题信息尚未加载完全。项目包括1个代码库，没有分支、归档或镜像。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Xbox One游戏是否可以在Windows PC上运行以及新功能的作用

不同观点：
• 观点一（Klaster_1提出）：质疑该功能是否允许在Windows PC上运行Xbox One游戏。Klaster_1对该功能的具体作用感到困惑，表明需要更清晰的解释。
• 观点二（FlyingSheep回应）：解释该功能实际上是允许将Xbox One游戏流式传输到Windows 10/11 PC上，而不是直接在PC上运行游戏。这意味着玩家可以通过网络从Xbox主机上玩游戏，而不是在PC本地上运行这些游戏。

补充讨论：
• FlyingSheep进一步解释：提到这项功能的实际应用场景，即通过家庭网络从Xbox主机上串流游戏到PC，而不是让PC直接运行Xbox游戏。
• 技术细节：该功能依赖于网络连接的质量，强调了网络在流式传输体验中的重要性。
• 争议焦点：主要争议在于用户对功能理解的偏差，一些用户期望能够在PC本地运行Xbox One游戏，而实际上仅支持流式传输。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国与其他国家之间的关税计算及其合理性

不同观点：
• **amscanne** 认为不需要通过逆向工程来理解美国关税计算，并提供了一个链接（https://ustr.gov/issue-areas/reciprocal-tariff-calculations）作为参考，表明这些信息是公开可查的。
  
• **jmeyer2k** 对关税计算持嘲讽态度，提到ChatGPT也曾建议类似的计算方法，暗示这是马斯克的一个“天才”想法。同时，通过一个链接（https://xcancel.com/krishnanrohit/status/1907587352157106292）调侃马达加斯加对美国进口商品征收47%的关税是合理的。

• **sayasen** 对关税调整持支持态度，质疑为什么调整关税使其更符合其他国家的有效税率会被认为是不好的做法，认为这只是让美国的关税与其他国家更一致。

• **protocolture** 对关税调整持强烈反对态度，使用“monumentally dumb”来形容这个想法，表现出对此话题的强烈负面情绪，虽然没有提供具体论据，但显然对此非常不满。

- sayasen 试图从逻辑和数据角度为关税调整辩护，但遭到protocolture的情感化强烈反对，显示出讨论中理性分析与情感反应之间的张力。
- 争议的焦点在于关税调整是否合理，特别是对美国与其他国家关税率的比较以及这种调整的潜在影响。

data.title: AmigaOS 3.2 Update 3 Released
data.author: codewiz
data.article_summary: Hyperion Entertainment CVBA宣布为AmigaOS 3.2提供第三次免费更新。此次更新包含了对OS 3.2.2长达两年的修复和增强，主要亮点包括：ReAction类的多项更新，TextEditor支持自定义菜单和宏，不再保留12 KB芯片RAM，以及新的Kickstart 3.2.3 ROM。此外，还包括对DiskDoctor和HDToolbox等至少50项其他问题的修复。注册用户可在此下载更新。感谢用户对AmigaOS的支持。

data.title: AutoGDB: exploit a binary while sipping coffee
data.author: retr0reg
data.article_summary: AutoGDB是一款GDB插件，通过SaaS方式实现客户端-服务器-客户端通信，允许在一个GDB中部署并随处使用。主要功能包括使用MCP（通过SSE协议）连接GDB和LLM（如OpenAI的Cursor），实现漏洞利用和调试。安装步骤包括使用curl一键安装AutoGDB，配置GDB连接和MCP代理，并设置LLM客户端以连接至AutoGDB。目前处于MVP阶段，仅OpenAI Agent SDK和Cursor支持其MCP via SSE功能。如有问题或建议，可联系AutoGDB团队。

43562637.article_content:
Exploit a binary using your LLM.
Signin to Exploit
Latest AutoGDB demo showcasing recent features.
How AutoGDB Works
AutoGDB's MCP works in a special way
. It use a SaaS-ish way to establish client-server-client communication, in order for that to work, I did some reworking and tweaking on the original MCP SSE Protocols session pool
(if you look closely, you can see the AutoGDB's MCP actually use SSE URL Paramter to connect)
. Which allows you to deploy AutoGDB in one GDB, and use it anywhere.
GDB plugin <--> command middleware <-> backend <-> MCP Backend <-> your LLM
0x01
GDB Setup
Curl
Wget
Manual
One-line installation using curl:
curl -s http://apollo.autogdb.io/download/autogdb.py > ~/.autogdb.py && echo "# AutoGDB MCP Config" >> ~/.gdbinit && echo "source ~/.autogdb.py" >> ~/.gdbinit
0x02
Generate & Connect
Sign in to Hack
Connect GDB
MCP Connection
In your GDB session (after installing the plugin):
autogdb connect http://apollo.autogdb.io YOUR_CONNECTION_ID
Generate a Connection ID above first.
0x03
Configure MCP Proxy
Install the `mcp-proxy` tool and configure your LLM client (like Cursor) to connect.
1. Install Proxy
Install `mcp-proxy` using one of the following methods:
UV
Pipx
uv tool install mcp-proxy

data.title: Four decades not sleeping well – until a doctor took my insomnia seriously
data.author: wheels
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者长达四十年与失眠症斗争的经历。从九岁起，作者就饱受失眠困扰，但每次向医生求助时，都被认为问题出在心理上，只需放松或通过泡澡、瑜伽等方法缓解。作者强调，失眠并非如一些医生所认为的只是女性的无理抱怨，而是一种可能危及生命的生理问题。经过多年被误解和忽视，作者终于在45岁时找到一位认真对待她病情的医生。文章还指出，睡眠问题与心理健康密切相关，许多美国人正面临失眠和抑郁的困扰。作者呼吁社会正视失眠的严重性，而不再简单归咎于情绪或性格问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：上气道阻力综合征（UARS）的普遍性与诊断不足问题，以及与阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停综合征（OSA）的区别。

不同观点：
• Llamamoe认为UARS非常常见且常被漏诊，因为大多数睡眠研究仅筛查睡眠呼吸暂停，且许多医生不了解UARS的不同表现形式。UARS和OSA在本质上是同一类疾病，但表现和严重程度可能不同。
  
• Llamamoe指出UARS和OSA的区别在于身体对气道塌陷的反应方式。OSA患者会在血氧饱和度下降时继续睡觉，而UARS患者则会醒来以重新建立气道通畅。虽然长期低氧血症的损害更大，但短期症状上，UARS的睡眠片段化问题更严重。

补充讨论：
• UARS可能在有鼻呼吸困难、下颌后缩或非常狭窄、夜间口呼吸以及睡眠受干扰的人群中更为常见。
• OSA更为常见于男性、肥胖人群和老年人，而UARS则在女性、年轻人和体型较瘦的人群中更为普遍。

争议焦点：UARS与OSA的诊断标准和临床表现的差异，以及医生对这两种疾病的认知不足，导致UARS的漏诊问题。这涉及到医疗系统在睡眠障碍筛查方面的局限性和改进需求。

Composite: The Guardian/Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
‘For nearly 40 years, every doctor I’ve pleaded with has announced that the problem is in my head.’
Composite: The Guardian/Getty Images
Well actually
I spent four decades not sleeping a wink – until a doctor took my insomnia seriously
Insomnia is not a grievance made by difficult women. It’s a life-threatening condition that often stems from a physical issue many doctors refuse to see
Courtney Maum
Wed 2 Apr 2025 06.00 EDT
Last modified on Wed 2 Apr 2025 13.12 EDT
Share
I
n February, I taught memoir writing at a conference in Mexico where the faculty is traditionally put up with local hosts. Mine was especially communicative in the months leading up to my arrival, going out of his way to indicate affordable rooftop bars, the finest locations to view murals, and general best practices for the city he’d adopted as his own.
So when I told my host that I have chronic insomnia, I felt he’d take me seriously, given how generous he’d been in his emails. “I’ve traveled a lot throughout Mexico,” I wrote him. “And the one thing I can’t deal with as an insomniac is roosters.”
There was a rooster in the vicinity, my host admitted, but it was way off in the distance and shouldn’t be a problem; his home had thick walls and was well insulated against noise.
Color me surprised when I arrived, a few hours shy of midnight, to the news that the rooster had recently relocated to the tree outside the guest bedroom where I’d be staying for the week. “He starts crowing at 4am,” my host explained, “and he just keeps on going.”
I clock up to 20,000 steps a night: my life with restless legs syndrome
Read more
“He’s lucky we’re vegetarians!” joked a visiting friend of his.
I went to bed disheartened and prematurely anxious. In addition to teaching a full load of courses, I had a novel under consideration at several publishing houses, so my week was jammed with high-stakes editorial calls. I can barely sleep with someone breathing next to me, so there wasn’t a chance in hell I’d be able to sleep through a rooster crowing outside my window.
After a sleepless night, I fled the coop on day two, relocating to a poultry-free hotel nearby, which made me feel guilty – the host had been so kind. I was also frustrated, knowing he probably thought I was exaggerating, using the word “insomniac” to stand in for “sensitive”.
When I tell people that I have immense trouble with sleep, what they hear is that I’m difficult, neurotic, a diva with control issues. For nearly 40 years, every doctor I’ve pleaded with has announced that the problem is in my head. That I need to relax, take hot baths, do a lot of yoga. Or, you know, go back and be born a man, because ladies are
high
-strung
.
But last year, at 45, I finally found a doctor who listened to my conviction that there was a physical root to my ailment.
This is the story of how I got through his office door.
As anyone trying to get through the day after a sleepless night will know, mental health is strongly linked to sleep satisfaction – and Americans are doing poorly in both of these departments.
A 2023 poll by the
National Sleep Foundation
found that “one in four adults who were dissatisfied with their sleep also met probable criteria for a depression diagnosis,” with women and the elderly suffering from insomnia, depression and
a reliance on sleeping aids
more than any other demographic. Last year, a fresh survey by the
American Academy of Sleep Medicine
announced that 12% of Americans had been diagnosed with chronic insomnia, the very condition I’m up against.
The message that I was overly sensitive, persistently hormonal and ‘keyed up’ was drilled into me so many times by doctors of both genders
My struggles with disordered sleeping started far younger than the national average. By age nine, I had entered the pattern I’m currently entrenched in – I could fall asleep but couldn’t stay asleep, usually waking up at about 4.30am, exhausted and disgruntled, unable to lure the sandman back.
I don’t think I knew the word “insomnia” at the time, but I knew something had shifted inside me for the worse. My home life was in shambles – my younger brother was suffering frequent, terrifying seizures and the stress of his undiagnosed illness was crumbling my parents’ already fractured marriage. When I complained to my mother about my sleep troubles, she gave me a “join the club” look. She brought home a pack of Sleepytime tea, but it only made me jealous of the narcoleptic brown bear on the packaging who could fall asleep wherever: in a lounger, in a hammock, in a field of chamomile.
The tea was the extent of my mother’s efforts to “deal” with my insomnia. My father doesn’t do emotions, so I stored up my complaints for the doctors I saw annually, giddy with the knowledge that they’d know how to “fix” me. My pediatrician, my dentist, the gynecologi

data.title: The NaNoWriMo organization is shutting down
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: NaNoWriMo（全国小说写作月）在运营超过20年后，因多年财务困境宣布关闭，将不再举办其年度写作挑战活动。该非营利组织在1999年由21位作家发起，2022年有超过40万作家参与。2023年，由于未明确反对AI写作工具及一名管理员涉及不当行为，NaNoWriMo遭到社区批评，参与人数和筹款减少。尽管官网将继续运行，但将不再组织正式的写作活动。组织表示，这对写作社区是重大损失，但仍对未来抱有希望。作家们仍可在11月自行挑战写小说或寻找其他替代活动。

News
The NaNoWriMo organization is shutting down
NaNoWriMo will no longer offer its annual challenge ‘after years of financial struggle.’
NaNoWriMo will no longer offer its annual challenge ‘after years of financial struggle.’
by
Emma Roth
Apr 2, 2025, 10:00 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Image: Hugo Herrera / The Verge
Emma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
NaNoWriMo (National Novel Writing Month)is shutting down after more than 20 years of hosting its annual challenge for writers. In
a video
and an
email
sent to community members, the nonprofit organization explains that it can no longer continue “after years of financial struggles.”
Before officially becoming a nonprofit in 2006, NaNoWriMo started out with
just 21 writers in 1999
. More than
400,000 writers participated
in NaNoWriMo’s programs that challenged people to finish writing a novel within the month of November in 2022.
In 2023, many writers abandoned NaNoWriMo
after it refused to take a stand against
the use of AI tools in writing. Around the same time, one of its moderators
faced child grooming accusations
, leading to more criticism from the community.
As shown in the video, NaNoWriMo interim executive director Kilby Blades details how participation and fundraising in the program have decreased in recent years. The NaNoWriMo site will remain online for “as long as possible,” though it will no longer formally host its writing challenges.
“We recognize that the closure of NaNoWriMo represents a huge loss to the writing community, and that grief over this outcome will be exacerbated by the challenges of the past sixteen months,” NaNoWriMo’s email to the community says. “This is not the ending that anybody wanted or planned. And—believe us—if we could hit the delete button and rewrite this last chapter, we would. But we do have hope for the epilogue.”
Even with the closure of NaNoWriMo, writers can still challenge themselves to write a novel during November. Or,
they can try out an alternative
.

data.author: bavarianbob

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare的WAF规则集更改导致包含"camel"的URL被误拦截的问题

不同观点：
• [tom_usher] 指出Cloudflare管理的WAF规则集发生了变化，任何使用该规则的网站都会因为'Apache Camel - Remote Code Execution - CVE:CVE-29891'规则而阻止包含'camel'的URL。受此问题影响的网站可以通过覆盖该规则来解决。

• [Recursing] 提供了更多受影响的例子，如npm和yarn上的相关路径，并提到npm团队已经确认了该事件，且问题已解决，提供了状态更新链接。

• [pvg] 提到这并不是Cloudflare WAF第一次出现问题，引用了一个之前的例子来证明其偶尔会引发问题。

• [miyuru] 讨论了WAF外包的利弊，认为像GitHub或微软这样的大公司应该有自己的WAF团队，而不是依赖外包产品。

• [klysm] 认为将安全作为附加产品购买会带来问题，暗示这种做法可能不够可靠。

• [mplanchard] 表达了对问题确认的欣慰，暗示之前因为此问题感到困惑。

• [drusepth] 询问unpkg的异常是否也与该问题有关，暗示问题影响范围可能更广。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Cloudflare WAF规则误拦截的频繁性和影响范围，以及外包WAF的优缺点。
• 提供了具体事件的链接和讨论，如npm的状态更新和之前类似问题的例子，帮助理解问题的背景和解决情况。

data.title: Flame – BBS and MUD
data.author: shakna
data.article_summary: Flame是一个公告板系统（BBS），虽然通过MUD（多用户迷宫游戏）形式实现，但它并非MUD、IRC或聊天室。对不同的人来说，Flame具有多种功能：可以 silent 访问，作为社交替代，灵魂探索之地或虚拟派对区。要连接Flame，可通过telnet访问flame.ucc.gu.uwa.edu.au的4242端口；若受防火墙限制，可使用flame-tunnel.ucc.gu.uwa.edu.au的任意端口。Flame还运行gopher服务器和web服务器。它始于1990年，最初是远程访问BBS，1991年出现在《Your Computer》杂志上，1992年转变为MUD，并保留了原BBS的电话连接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于MUD（多用户地牢）及相关技术的讨论，包括历史、使用体验、怀旧情感以及技术应用前景。

不同观点：
• [01100011] 认为该描述类似于Citadel BBS系统，并提到20世纪80年代太平洋西北地区（PNW）BBS的繁荣，指出由于天气原因，该地区技术发展迅速。
• [JKCalhoun] 提到在MacOS上使用telnet访问MUD的实际操作步骤，并分享了90年代对网络空间（cyberpunk）故事场景的想象，描述了在MUD酒吧中进行秘密会谈的场景。
• [khimaros] 表达了对GhostMOO（一个具体的MUD）的怀旧，提到该MUD曾经充满玩家，并询问是否还有其他人怀念那段时光。
• [captaincrunch] 表示对讨论内容的部分不理解，语气中带有困惑。
• [upghost] 对MUD作为在线社交空间的形式表示赞赏，并希望这种形式能更普遍。
• [kaiyuanzg] 从技术角度出发，讨论了Flame作为集群管理工具的潜力，并将其与Cloudify和OpenStack等解决方案进行比较，表现出对技术发展前景的关注。

补充讨论：
• 怀旧情感：[khimaros] 和 [JKCalhoun] 都表现出对过去网络文化和MUD游戏的怀念，前者具体提到GhostMOO，后者则构想了一个网络空间故事场景。
• 技术操作：[JKCalhoun] 提供了在MacOS上使用telnet访问MUD的具体步骤，增加了讨论的技术深度。
• 技术前景：[kaiyuanzg] 关注Flame的技术应用前景，特别是与Cloudify和OpenStack等现有解决方案的比较，体现了对技术发展的关注。

争议焦点：
• 讨论中并无明显争议，但[captaincrunch]对部分内容表示不解，可能反映了讨论中技术细节和背景知识的不对称。

data.title: Preventing nearsightedness using AR glasses or projectors
data.author: plun9
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了预防近视的方法，特别是针对长时间使用电脑和手机等近距离设备导致的问题。传统建议是经常休息并眺望远处，但这在实际操作中可能不现实。文章提出了几种替代方案：

1. **微显示设备（如VR/AR头显）**：这些设备让眼睛聚焦在2-4米远的图像上，避免长时间近距离用眼，减轻近视风险。虽然VR头显价格较高、电池续航有限且长时间使用可能不适，但AR眼镜更为舒适，并能模拟大工作空间。

2. **投影仪**：使用投影仪将内容投射到墙上，图像大小可超过100英寸，眼睛聚焦距离更远，有助于保护视力。配合抗光幕和高短投投影仪效果更佳。

这些方法通过让眼睛保持放松，减少近视的发生和发展。

43531734.article_content:
03/31/25
Preventing Nearsightedness
Nearsightedness (myopia) is on the rise. Around the
world, billions of people have the disease, and it is expected that the
population with the disease will continue to grow. We all use computers,
phones, and perhaps read books and look at other content every day,
perhaps for extended periods of time.
Estimated myopia rate in 20-year-olds in Asia
by The RedBurn under CC BY 4.0
You've probably learned of a way to prevent nearsightedness, which is by
taking breaks periodically and looking at distant objects. It's valid
but perhaps impractical. If you are a knowledge worker, during a typical
workday, you would need to plan and allocate time for 15 or more breaks,
which is difficult to do when you're trying to concentrate on your work.
Alternative Solutions
You can prevent nearsightedness simply by not focusing on near objects
for long periods of time. You could avoid computer monitors and physical
books entirely. But what could you use instead?
Microdisplays (AR/VR)
Microsoft HoloLens Bloom Gesture
by Kai Kowalewski under CC BY 4.0
While using microdisplay-equipped devices, your eyes stay relaxed
because they're focused at an image that is 2-4 meters away. This
prevents nearsightedness induced by focusing on close objects for long
periods of time. Nowaways, VR headsets are becoming more popular. They
are typically used for gaming, but you can use a VR headset as a
computing platform, like with the Apple Vision Pro. You can also use
them like a computer monitor or as a remote display. Unfortunately, VR
headsets can be expensive, have limited battery life, and become
uncomfortable to use after long periods of time. An alternative is to
use another type of device with microdisplays: AR glasses. As with VR
headsets, your eyes will stay relaxed as you use the device.
The screen can  appear to be at a size of 126" at a distance of 4
meters away, for instance. Unfortunately, at the moment, screen resolution remains limited to 1080p
for the latest AR glasses. Additional software can allow you to simulate
a large workspace with multiple monitors. AR glasses are comfortable to
use for multiple hours at a time, meaning you don't necessarily need to
take breaks if you don't want to.
Projection
If you have the space, you could use a projector to project content from
a computer or some other device onto a wall or projector screen. The
content could be displayed at a size that's larger than most TVs, from
90 to 130". A large size and high resolution are important factors
in preserving the large workspace of a standard computer monitor for
productivity. Like
with microdisplay devices, your eyes will be focused on an image that is
several meters away as opposed to a typical computer monitor. For better
results during the day, you could use an ambient light rejecting (ALR)
projection screen. You can pair an ALR screen with an ultra-short throw
(UST) projector for better results. In order to simulate a multi-monitor
setup, you could use multiple projectors, or perhaps a TV beside the
projector screen.

data.title: Mirrors: The Blind Spot of Image and Video Generation Models
data.author: yamrzou
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了图像和视频生成模型在处理镜子反射时的挑战。作者评估了五种图像生成模型（如Gemini、Adobe Firefly、Bing等）和四种视频生成模型（如veed.io、pollo.ai等），使用包含人物和物体的五个提示场景。结果显示，这些模型在生成准确的镜像反射时普遍存在问题，如反射缺失、变形或不一致。例如，Gemini模型在处理猫、椅子和厨房场景时出现错误，Ideogram模型在处理群体图像和面部时也出现显著错误。视频模型则不仅在静态反射上存在问题，还在动态反射的一致性上表现不佳。文章指出，解决这一盲点对于提升生成内容的真实性和物理合理性至关重要。

43536879.article_content:
Mirrors: The Blind Spot of Image and Video Generation Models
Ali Borji
·
Follow
5 min read
·
Feb 10, 2025
--
Listen
Share
Recent advances in image generation models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in creating photorealistic and imaginative visuals. However, a persistent challenge remains:
accurately rendering reflections in mirrors
. We anecdotally evaluate five image generation models and four video generation models using five prompts featuring both humans and objects. Our findings reveal that AI models frequently struggle with reflections, often generating distorted, inconsistent, or entirely incorrect images. Here is the
data
.
Image generated by Gemini for the prompt: “An image of two cats playing in front of a mirror”
Introduction
Generative image models, particularly those based on deep learning, have achieved impressive results in synthesizing realistic images of various scenes and objects. From generating human faces to creating fantastical landscapes, these models have shown a remarkable ability to learn complex data distributions and produce novel content. However, despite their progress, a seemingly simple element — the mirror — continues to pose a significant challenge. Reflections, governed by the precise laws of optics, often appear distorted, misplaced, or entirely absent in generated images. This article explores how mirrors pose a significant challenge for generative models and suggests that addressing this blind spot is crucial to achieve more realistic and physically plausible image synthesis.
Experiments and Results
We chose a range of generative models to assess how effectively popular image and video generation models can synthesize content with accurate mirror reflections. These models are readily available to the public.
Image generation models
We evaluated five image generation models including:
Gemini which uses Imagen 3 as its generation backbone
Adobe Firefly
Bing which uses DALL-E 3
Ideogram
Freepik.com
These models were evaluated using the following prompts, some featuring humans and others containing only objects.
An image of a young lady holding a pen in front of a mirror
An image of two cats playing in front of a mirror
An image of a chair in front of a mirror
An image of a group of people in a room with a mirror in it
An image of a kitchen with a mirror in it
The results from various models (some examples are shown below) show consistent patterns of reflection and perspective issues. The Gemini model struggles with incorrect or missing reflections and misjudged object placements, particularly with cats, chairs, and kitchen scenes. Some errors are subtle but noticeable.
The Ideogram model generally produces higher fidelity images, but also faces recurring issues. Hand reflections are often incorrect, and objects can appear inconsistently reflected. It particularly struggles with group images and faces, making significant errors in reflections and image coherence. Quality of faces in group images is poor.
Adobe Firefly has more severe errors, such as objects extending unnaturally outside mirrors and misaligned or missing reflections, leading to reduced realism.
Bing Image Creator often produces cartoonish images with significant reflection issues, misplacing or distorting elements.
Freepik-generated cat images show high visual quality but still suffer from similar reflection errors, highlighting a common challenge across models.
Image generated by Ideogram for the prompt: “An image of two cats playing in front of a mirror”
Image generated by Ideogram for the prompt: “An image of a chair in front of a mirror”
Image generated by Ideogram for the prompt: “An image of a kitchen with a mirror in it”
Image generated by Ideogram for the prompt: “An image of a young lady holding a pen in front of a mirror”
Image generated by Ideogram for the prompt: “An image of a group of people in a room with a mirror in it”
Image generated by Adobe for the prompt: “An image of a young lady holding a pen in front of a mirror”
High-resolution versions of the generated images are available on the GitHub page associated with this article for further examination.
Video generation models
Additionally, we evaluated the following text-to-video generation models using only the first prompt from the previous subsection.
veed.io
pollo.ai (poolo 1.5)
ltx.studio
vidnoz.com
These models exhibit similar issues to those observed in the image generation models. In addition to errors in appearance and consistency, they also struggle with
accurately generating motion in reflections.
Reflected elements often move incorrectly or fail to correspond to the real-world physics of mirrored motion, further degrading the realism of the generated videos. As a result, their overall performance in handling reflections is particularly poor, making the generated videos noticeably flawed.

data.title: Nelm, a Helm 3 alternative, is generally available now
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Nelm 是一个 Helm 3 的替代工具，用于管理 Helm Charts 并将其部署到 Kubernetes。它是 werf 项目的部署引擎，具有多项增强功能，包括类似 `terraform plan` 的能力、使用服务端应用（Server-Side Apply）替代三向合并（3-Way Merge）、 secrets 管理、高级资源排序、改进的资源状态跟踪和日志打印等。Nelm 基于改进的 Helm 3 代码库，修复了 Helm 3 的多个 bug，并提供了更多高级特性，如加密值和文件、资源依赖管理等。用户可以通过其 CLI 进行安装和快速入门，具体操作可参考其 GitHub 页面。

Nelm
is a Helm 3 alternative. It is a Kubernetes deployment tool that manages Helm Charts and deploys them to Kubernetes and also is the deployment engine of
werf
. It can do (almost) everything that Helm does, but better, and even quite some on top of it. Nelm is based on improved and partially rewritten Helm 3 codebase, to introduce:
terraform plan
-like capabilities;
replacement of 3-Way Merge with Server-Side Apply;
secrets management;
advanced resource ordering capabilities;
improved resource state/error tracking;
continuous printing of logs, events, resource statuses, and errors during deployment;
lots of fixes for Helm 3 bugs, e.g.
"no matches for kind Deployment in version apps/v1beta1"
;
... and more.

43566389.article_summary: Nelm 是一个 Helm 3 的替代工具，用于管理 Helm Charts 并将其部署到 Kubernetes。它是 werf 项目的部署引擎，具有多项增强功能，包括类似 `terraform plan` 的能力、使用服务端应用（Server-Side Apply）替代三向合并（3-Way Merge）、 secrets 管理、高级资源排序、改进的资源状态跟踪和日志打印等。Nelm 基于改进的 Helm 3 代码库，修复了 Helm 3 的多个 bug，并提供了更多高级特性，如加密值和文件、资源依赖管理等。用户可以通过其 CLI 进行安装和快速入门，具体操作可参考其 GitHub 页面。

data.title: .NET library MassTransit going commercial with V9
data.author: 8-prime
data.article_summary: MassTransit宣布推出v9版本，并转向商业许可模式。这一变化旨在确保项目的长期可持续性、持续创新和提供企业级支持。MassTransit v8将继续保持开源，并提供安全补丁和关键错误修复。v9版本将引入新功能和性能增强，通过商业许可提供，并针对不同规模的组织提供支持计划。过渡计划包括2025年Q3发布v9预览版，2026年Q1正式发布。现有v8用户可继续使用，也可选择商业支持和v9的创新功能。具体价格和更多细节将在后续公布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源软件转向商业许可的争议及其对.NET生态系统的影响

不同观点：
• [fabian2k] 认为商业许可的主要问题不在于付费，而在于定价模式不透明，可能由于高昂的费用导致某些用例无法实施。此外，理解许可条款和处理企业内部官僚程序也增加了额外的负担。许可变更总是令人烦恼，因为在最初选择时无法做出明智的决定，而且未来价格模式可能会再次改变。

• [000ooo000] 关注v9的非商业许可问题，指出v8的支持将持续到2026年底，开发者有足够时间规划迁移。同时批评FAQ未直接回答问题，显得不专业。

• [xnorswap] 提到安全补丁和关键错误修复会在过渡期内继续提供，但未明确过渡期时长。以往案例如IdentityServer的许可变更导致许多企业不愿采用商业许可，并继续使用旧版本。即使在安全关键部分，旧版本仍被广泛使用。

• [Lachstec] 感到遗憾，认为.NET生态系统过于企业化，开源未得到应有的重视，尽管C#和.NET是优秀的工具。

• [pjmlp] 指出开源库的作者也需要支付账单，支持他们的商业努力。

• [hatly22] 猜测模糊的定价解释可能是为了吸引工具制造商或微软的收购。

• [poilcn] 希望能有可行的开源分支，因为非财务原因也可能导致排除商业许可。

• [_hao] 个人不喜欢MassTransit，认为其过于固执己见，倾向于使用更直接的SDK并减少代码依赖。对.NET OSS现状感到失望，认为其在精神和实践上已经回归到.NET框架时代。

• [DimmieMan] 认为这是开源软件的失败，支持他们的商业努力，但对.NET OSS的未来感到担忧，认为可能会导致开发者回归微软包。

• [DeathArrow] 表示不在意许可变化，因为在实际项目中一直直接使用如RabbitMQ、NATS、Kafka等服务。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于开源项目转向商业许可对开发者和企业的潜在影响，尤其是定价不透明和旧版本持续使用问题。
• 对.NET生态系统未来发展的担忧，特别是开源精神是否能够持续。
• 不同开发者的实际需求和偏好，如对MassTransit的看法和直接使用底层SDK的倾向。

43565690.article_content:
Announcing MassTransit v9
A New Era for Enterprise Messaging
For over a decade, MassTransit has been the leading open-source .NET messaging framework, trusted by thousands developers and enterprises worldwide to build
scalable, distributed applications. It has facilitated billions of transactions, powered mission-critical systems in finance, healthcare, government, and
logistics, and seamlessly integrated with cloud platforms like Microsoft Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud. As adoption has surged and enterprise demand has grown,
MassTransit has evolved into a cornerstone of modern event-driven architectures. Today, we’re excited to share an important milestone!
Update - post announcement Q&A added
below
We are transitioning to a commercial model.
With MassTransit v9, we are transitioning to a commercial licensing model. This change ensures long-term sustainability, continued innovation, and
enterprise-grade support — while leaving MassTransit v8 open-source and available to the community.
Why the Change?
When MassTransit first started in 2007, it was a single assembly that supported MSMQ. Fast-forward to today, and MassTransit has extensive support for several
message brokers, multiple databases, powerful capabilities including saga state machines, job consumers, message scheduling, and routing slips, as well as its
own SQL-based message transport. The entire solution builds and deploys over thirty NuGet packages.
Because of its extensive capabilities, MassTransit has grown into a mission-critical foundation for organizations worldwide. Trusted by enterprises in more than
100 countries across industries including finance, healthcare, logistics, and government. As adoption has surged, so has the need for:
Dedicated, full-time development resources to enhance and maintain the platform.
Enterprise-grade support and guarantees for business-critical applications.
A sustainable, long-term funding model to drive continuous innovation.
By making v9 a commercial release, we can accelerate MassTransit’s evolution, delivering even better scalability, security, and performance — while continuing
to support the existing community.
Change is Hard, Why Now?
We know that change — especially in the open-source world — can be challenging. If you’ve been relying on MassTransit as a free and open solution, you might be
wondering what this shift means for you and your team. We want to be clear: we deeply appreciate the community that has helped make MassTransit what it is
today. This decision wasn’t made lightly, but rather with the long-term success and sustainability of the project in mind.
By moving to a commercial model for v9, we’re ensuring that MassTransit can continue to evolve, with dedicated resources, faster development cycles, and the
enterprise support that many organizations have been asking for. MassTransit v8 remains open-source, and we’re committed to making this transition as smooth
as possible. Our goal isn’t to take something away — but to build something even better, with the stability and support that businesses need. We’re here to
help, and we welcome your questions, feedback, and thoughts as we move forward together.
What This Means for You
MassTransit v8 Remains Open Source
The existing v8 codebase will remain open-source and available under its current license.
Security patches and critical bug fixes will continue for a transition period.
Community support remains available for v8 users.
MassTransit v9 Becomes a Commercial Product
New features, performance enhancements, and enterprise-focused capabilities will be exclusive to v9.
Available via a commercial license with support plans tailored for organizations of all sizes, including rates for independent software vendors and
consultants building and
supporting their own customer applications using MassTransit.
Expert assistance, SLAs, and long-term stability guarantees for enterprise users.
The Transition Plan
Moving to a commercial product is a huge undertaking, and the initial target dates for the transition are outlined below (and are subject to change).
Date
Milestone
Q3 2025
MassTransit v9 prerelease packages available to early adopters.
Q1 2026
MassTransit v9 official release under a commercial license.
Ongoing
MassTransit v8 security patches and community support continue.
After 2026
End of official maintenance for MassTransit v8.
How Do I Prepare?
If you're currently using MassTransit v8:
You can continue using v8 with no changes — it's open-source and will remain available.
If you need commercial support,
support agreements
are available.
If you want access to v9 and future innovations, consider our commercial licensing options (to be announced at a later date).
If you currently have a support agreement:
You will be granted a license for MassTransit v9 through the remainder of your support period.
Support will continue for your existing MassTransit v8 applications.

data.title: National security adviser Michael Waltz reportedly conducted business via Gmail
data.author: beardyw
data.article_summary: 美国国家安全顾问迈克尔·沃尔兹被曝使用个人Gmail处理政府事务，进一步引发安全担忧。此前，他曾因将一名记者误加入涉及也门空袭计划的Signal群聊而受到批评。据《华盛顿邮报》披露，沃尔兹通过Gmail接收工作日程等敏感信息，其助手也被指用Gmail讨论军事位置和武器系统。尽管白宫国安会发言人否认不当使用Gmail，但这一事件再次引发对沃尔兹的质疑。民主党人呼吁沃尔兹及其同僚辞职，但特朗普称此事为“小故障”，拒绝解雇沃尔兹。此前，沃尔兹曾批评希拉里·克林顿使用私人邮箱处理国务事务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[对政府邮箱使用Gmail及相关安全问题的讨论]

不同观点：
• LinuxBender认为，许多.gov邮箱实际上是转发到Gmail的，并对此表示担忧。他希望这些是企业账户，并且至少启用了双重认证（2FA）。他还建议对所有.gov邮箱进行审计，以确认其路由和加密状态，确保符合政府的分类标准。

• Havoc对此事件提出质疑，认为如果这种情况存在，那么相关部门是否具备足够的专业能力来处理敏感信息，并提到这一问题涉及国家安全顾问，进一步突显了问题的严重性。

• Edgineer引用了Waltz的案例，指出虽然有“潜在可利用信息”被发送至Gmail，但并未明确说明Waltz本人是否使用了该账户发送信息。同时，对助手使用Gmail处理敏感信息的指控比较模糊。

• Chromehearts仅表达了对这一情况的情感反应，认为这是令人尴尬的，但没有进一步展开讨论。

• ChrisArchitect提供了相关讨论的早期来源链接，引导读者查看更多背景信息。

• Peterlada用简短的语句“Lock him up”（把他关起来），表达了对事件责任人应受惩罚的强烈情绪。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到的安全问题包括：.gov邮箱是否应该转发至Gmail，双重认证的使用情况，以及对敏感信息的加密和分类处理是否合规。
• 部分评论对相关人员使用非官方邮箱处理敏感信息的做法表示强烈不满，认为这可能威胁国家安全。
• 讨论中也包含了一些情绪化的表达，如“ embarrassing”和“Lock him up”，反映了公众对此类事件的强烈反应。

Trump administration
National security adviser Michael Waltz reportedly conducted business via Gmail
Latest security flap again focuses scrutiny on Waltz after he earlier added journalist to Yemen war-planning chat
Oliver Milman
in New York
Wed 2 Apr 2025 11.32 EDT
Last modified on Wed 2 Apr 2025 20.14 EDT
Share
Michael Waltz, the embattled national security adviser to
Donald Trump
, and other members of the national security council have reportedly used personal
Gmail
accounts to conduct government business.
The apparent use of Gmail, a relatively insecure method of communication for high-level government officials, places further scrutiny upon Waltz, who is already
under pressure
after adding a journalist to a group chat on the commercial
Signal app
, where top US officials then planned and celebrated a US airstrike in
Yemen
last month.
The revelations of the Gmail use
come from the Washington Post
, which said it has reviewed documents and interviewed three unnamed officials about the apparent security lapse.
Waltz had “potentially exploitable information” sent to his
Gmail
, such as his schedule and other work documents, the Post reported.
US justice department drops corruption case against New York mayor Eric Adams
Read more
One of Waltz’s aides on the national security council, meanwhile, allegedly used Gmail for more sensitive material, such as discussing military positions and weapons systems with colleagues in other government agencies who used their government-issued accounts.
A spokesperson for the national security council denied to the Post that Waltz had used Gmail improperly. “Waltz didn’t and wouldn’t send classified information on an open account,” the spokesperson said.
This latest episode, however, risks further damage to the standing of Waltz following the revelation last week that he added Jeffrey Goldberg, editor-in-chief of the Atlantic magazine, to
a Signal group chat
that involved senior figures such as
JD Vance
, the US vice-president, and
Pete Hegseth
, the defense secretary, that discussed details of an airstrike upon the Houthi rebel group in Yemen.
Waltz has said that Goldberg’s number was somehow “sucked in” to his phone, a comment that drew scorn from Goldberg and others. Trump has, however, declined to fire Waltz, instead calling the incident a “glitch”.
Prior to his role as the president’s national security adviser, Waltz was highly critical of Hillary Clinton for her use of a private email server when she was secretary of state.
